papers.abstract: As cubic GaN is a promising material for optoelectronic applications, its layers need to be precisely doped to realize the desired properties. While contact-based methods are established to measure the realized charge carrier density, contact-free techniques are more advantageous for this purpose. We show terahertz time-domain spectroscopy measurements of cubic GaN layers with thicknesses between 0.6 $μ$m and 2 $μ$m with doping densities in the range from $10^{18}$ cm$^{-3}$ to $10^{20}$ cm$^{-3}$. From these measurements, we determine the charge carrier densities and verify the results with time-of-flight secondary-ion mass spectrometry measurements. The results are in accordance with simulations of the doping ranges which the technique is expected to be sensitive in. In preparation for the terahertz time-domain spectroscopy measurements, we validated the layer thicknesses by Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy measurements. With this, a wide range of doped cubic GaN samples can be addressed by optical methods. In the future, these techniques could allow for a fast and non-destructive characterization of GaN layers, right after or even during the growth process.

papers.title: Mode Dynamics: A Framework for Neural Network Learning
papers.abstract: We introduce Mode Dynamics, a framework that connects coordinated parameter motion during neural network learning to changes in model outputs. Starting from a recorded parameter trajectory, we decompose its updates into collective modes and map each mode to its state-dependent output effect. The framework organizes this link through three mechanisms. Decomposition identifies collective modes in parameter motion and their time-varying amplitudes. Reconstruction tests whether the effects induced by those modes recover local and accumulated output change. Concentration quantifies how behavioral contribution is distributed across modes. Controlled scalar regression and next-token experiments directly test these mechanisms. They show that small sets of leading modes reconstruct behavior, induced effects depend on the training path, and modal complexity varies with task and data. We then evaluate the framework on held-out image and language-model outputs using CIFAR-100 autoencoding and a public Pythia-70M pretraining trajectory. Across these settings, the results connect compact modal subspaces of recorded parameter motion to evolving behavior.

papers.title: What kinds of strong star--black-hole encounters in AGN disks occur, and how often?
papers.abstract: Disks surrounding active galactic nuclei contain many stars and black holes, which will inevitably encounter one another. The outcome of these encounters depends on how closely and how rapidly the bodies meet. Extending previous studies, we account for initial relative velocities seeded by stochastic effects in the disk; incorporate a strong-encounter cross-section accounting for single- and binary-mediated interactions computed via direct two-body (Hill) or three-body (isolated) interactions; and present a repeated-encounter model accounting both for energy loss due to stellar encounters as well as the SMBH tidal field. We convolve our encounter model with a parametric family of natal stellar and binary populations, focused on varying binary fraction and period distribution. In our fiducial disk model, even though single-single interactions supply most encounters, binary-mediated interactions supply 68% of collisions; most encounters are well-approximated as parabolic; and stochastically-driven relative velocities are comparatively substantial and driven by gravitational perturbations from disk fluctuations and neighboring bodies. Our tools are ready to use in downstream applications, including several easily-expressed semianalytic approximations to key interaction phenomena.

papers.title: A lifted entropy splitting lemma and applications
papers.abstract: We give a matrix lifting of the entropy-splitting theorem of Csiszár, Körner, Lovász, Marton, and Simonyi, and show several applications. We use it to prove the Cartesian-product inequality conjectured by Sinjorgo and Sotirov for the generalized Lovász theta number, and we also answer the saturation and convexification questions of Carli Silva, Coutinho, Oliveira, and Tunçel on the same theme. For the strong Hoffman bound, we answer a question of Wocjan, Elphick, and Darbari concerning orthogonal rank, and show that optimization over matrix weights gives exactly the ceiling of the theta number of the complement. Finally, we extend the lifting to diagonally invariant cones of positive semidefinite matrices, giving a proof of a conjecture by Kuryatnikova, Sotirov, and Vera, and giving a short proof, for all graphs, of a theta-based weakening of Fajtlowicz's graph-energy conjecture.

papers.title: Unsupervised Feature Selection Using Local Intrinsic Dimensionality -- Extended Version
papers.abstract: High dimensionality degrades both the efficiency and the effectiveness of learning algorithms, and in many applications no class labels are available to guide dimensionality reduction. This paper proposes LIDFS, an unsupervised feature selection method based on Local Intrinsic Dimensionality (LID). The method builds on the formal equivalence between LID and the indiscriminability of distance measures. The data matrix is transposed so that each feature is treated as a point, and the LID of each feature is estimated by maximum likelihood from the distances to its $k$ nearest neighboring features. Features with lower LID exhibit greater local discriminability and receive higher importance scores. A refinement step then retains one representative per feature neighborhood and demotes locally redundant features. The result is a complete ranking from which any number of features can be selected without rerunning the procedure. LIDFS does not use any information about labels or the number of classes, and runs in $\mathcal{O}(d^2 n)$ time for $n$ instances and $d$ features. LIDFS is compared with classic and state-of-the-art methods and a random baseline on 23 high-dimensional datasets, the classic benchmark collection. The evaluation uses classification accuracy and AUC with five downstream classifiers, as well as clustering accuracy and normalized mutual information, over both full and aggressive selection ranges. LIDFS ranks first in the supervised evaluations and first or tied second in the clustering-based evaluations. It belongs to the top statistical group together with methods that require the number of classes, and it runs faster than its closest competitor. Several recent methods, by contrast, fail to outperform the random baseline. A sensitivity analysis shows that small neighborhood sizes yield the best results.

papers.title: Nearly Optimal Sparse Navigable Graphs in General Metrics
papers.abstract: We study approximation algorithms for constructing sparse navigable graphs in general metrics. Given an $n$-point metric $(P,d)$ and a parameter $α\ge1$, a directed graph on $P$ is $α$-navigable if, for every pair of distinct points $s,t\in P$, the source $s$ has an outgoing neighbor $p$ with $d(p,t)<d(s,t)/α$. The objective is to minimize the number of edges. Recent independent works of Khanna, Padaki, and Waingarten (2026) and Conway et al. (2026) give $O(\log n)$-approximation algorithms and show that an $o(\log n)$ approximation is NP-hard in general. Before our work, the best known running time for such an approximation for general $α\ge1$ was $\widetilde O(\min\{n\operatorname{OPT}_α,n^{2.5}\})$, where $\operatorname{OPT}_α$ is the minimum number of edges in an $α$-navigable graph. In this paper, we give a randomized algorithm that, with high probability, runs in $\widetilde O(n^2)$ time and achieves an $O(\log n)$ approximation for every $α\ge1$. In general, these guarantees are nearly optimal up to constant factors in the approximation and polylogarithmic factors in the running time.

papers.title: Dynamical relations on $\mathbb{P}^1$, higher bifurcations, and arithmetic bigness
papers.abstract: In this article, we study algebraic relations among rational maps on $\mathbb{P}^1$ and among their preperiodic points. Working over $\mathbb{C}$, we characterize algebraic families of positive-dimensional varieties in $(\mathbb{P}^1)^N$ and tuples of maps $(f_1, \ldots, f_N)$ for which the subvariety is dynamically special for a Zariski-dense set of parameters. Moreover, outside of well-understood elliptic phenomena, we show that all families of maps and subvarieties that bifurcate are maximally bifurcating. Working over $\overline{\mathbb{Q}}$, we characterize arithmetic and geometric potential bigness for the canonical line bundle associated to families of endomorphisms of $(\mathbb{P}^1)^N$ when restricted to the subvarieties. As consequences, we obtain uniform bounds for the periods and preperiods of relations among non-exceptional maps, and we show uniform bounds on the geometry of preperiodic points satisfying these relations. Over $\overline{\mathbb{Q}}$, our results yield corresponding uniform bounds for points and subvarieties satisfying a height gap.

papers.title: Compact and Hilbert-Schmidt composition operators on weighted Hardy spaces
papers.abstract: Lefèvre, Li, Queffélec, and Rodríguez-Piazza [12] recently characterized the sequences $β$ for which the weighted Hardy space $H^2(β)$ has the same bounded composition operators as the Hardy space $H^2$. We investigate the analogous questions for the compactness and the $p$-Schatten classes: for which sequences $β$ does the space $H^2(β)$ have the same compact or $p$-Schatten class composition operators as $H^2$?

papers.title: Spin-Orbit Coupling Response Theory within the Oriented Spin Space Group Framework
papers.abstract: Spin-orbit coupling (SOC) plays a pivotal role in a broad range of phenomena in condensed matter physics. The recently developed spin space group theory offers a new perspective for characterizing the fundamental symmetry-breaking features of SOC-related phenomena, yet its full potential remains to be explored. Here, we provide a general framework that relates the SOC-induced symmetry breaking to modifications of physical properties and emergence of new physical effects. This approach incorporates the recently developed oriented spin space group (OSSG) formalism, which can explicitly describe the symmetry reduction induced by SOC. By parameterizing the SOC Hamiltonian using a SOC tensor that connects real and spin spaces, an expansion in terms of the SOC components can be constructed for the response tensor describing any physical quantity. This framework determines not only whether a SOC-induced response is symmetry allowed, but also the lowest order in SOC at which it emerges and its dependence on magnetic anisotropy. As representative applications, we analyze the magnetoelectric coupling in Type-II multiferroics and show that magnetically induced electric polarization in different systems can be the result of SOC effects of different orders, and can exhibit varying characteristics of magnetic anisotropy. We further apply this theory to the anomalous Hall effect and spin magnetization in antiferromagnets, demonstrating that their distinct transformation properties under the OSSG allow a large anomalous Hall response to coexist with weak spin magnetization. A high-throughput analysis of materials in the MAGNDATA database identifies several symmetry-based material classes favorable for this coexistence. Overall, the proposed framework provides a unified symmetry description of SOC-induced phenomena and offers a systematic way for the identification of SOC-driven functional materials.

papers.title: Packing and covering random trees
papers.abstract: We study the sizes of optimal packings and coverings of conditioned branching processes by balls with growing radii. We find a universal limiting constant, and thereby establish universality of packing and covering numbers across different scales and different offspring distributions. To be precise, for $μ$ an offspring distribution with mean $1$ and finite variance $σ^2$ we let $T_n$ be a Bienaymé tree with offspring distribution $μ$ conditioned to have size $n$. We prove that the packing number (resp. covering number) of $T_n$ with balls of radii $1\ll γ_n \ll n^{1/2}$ is asymptotically equivalent to $\mathfrak{C} n /(σ^2 γ_n^2)$ (resp. $\mathfrak{C} n /(4σ^2 γ_n^2)$), for a universal constant $\mathfrak{C}$. We also show that the order of limits can be exchanged and that the same limit occurs when we first consider the limiting covering number of $T_n$ by balls of fixed radius $R$, and thereafter let $R$ tend to $\infty$. We then extend these results to the Brownian continuum random tree conditioned to have mass $1$. For this model, we prove that the packing (resp. covering) number with balls of radii $\varepsilon$ are asymptotically equivalent to $\mathfrak{C}/\varepsilon^2$ (resp. $\mathfrak{C}/(4\varepsilon^2)$), for the same constant $\mathfrak{C}$, in contrast with a conjecture by Aldous. Finally, our results answer a question by Devroye, Eide and Pralat on the asymptotic burning number of mean $1$ finite variance Bienaymé trees of size $n$, by showing that it lies between $(c+o(1)) n^{1/3}$ and $(2c+o(1))n^{1/3}$ with high probability, for a constant $c$ that only depends on the offspring variance.

papers.title: The generative paradox: the Anti-Prompt paradigm for human capability
papers.abstract: Generative AI in education is usually judged by the output of human-AI teams. That focus overlooks a second outcome: what people can still understand, challenge, repair, and adapt when assistance changes or disappears. We call this tension the generative paradox and distinguish four manifestations: performance, assistance, ownership, and capability stock. We propose developmental function allocation, which complements operational function allocation and meaningful human control by treating retained human capability as a design objective alongside current joint performance. The Anti-Prompt paradigm reverses the default interaction order: when immediate generation would preempt a consequential human act, AI should first create the conditions for human construction. We distinguish the validity of a product, responsibility for its construction, and evidence of capability after support changes. Representative Anti-Prompts, a canonical interaction sequence, and stress tests spanning mathematical reasoning, experimental science, software diagnosis, and lesson design make these distinctions concrete. We conclude with falsifiable predictions about retained capability and a system-level hypothesis about the reproduction and distribution of expertise.

papers.title: Non-Archimedean Rigidity and the Uniform Dynamical Manin--Mumford for $\left(\mathbb{P}^1\right)^n$
papers.abstract: We prove a uniform form of the dynamical Manin-Mumford conjecture for split endomorphisms $Φ= \left(f_1,\ldots,f_n\right): \left(\mathbb{P}^1\right)^n \to \left(\mathbb{P}^1\right)^n$ over $\mathbb{C}$, where each $f_i$ has degree $d \geq 2$ and at most one $f_i$ is exceptional. Specifically, we bound the number of irreducible components of $\overline{\operatorname{Prep}\left(Φ\right)\cap V\left(\mathbb{C}\right)}^{\operatorname{Zar}}$ uniformly, depending only on $\left(n,d,\operatorname{deg} V\right)$. We also obtain uniform statements for the dynamical Bogomolov conjecture. Our approach combines a degeneration argument via ultrafilters with a new non-archimedean rigidity theorem, along with the quantitative dynamical Zhang's inequality by Mavraki and the second author.

papers.title: Hierarchical Step Decomposition for Training-free Online Video Step Grounding
papers.abstract: Given a set of procedural steps, Video Step Grounding (VSG) aims to identify which steps occur in a video and localize when they are performed. Existing methods are either offline, requiring access to the full video before making predictions, or online, but relying on fixed-length video segments producing noisy, over-segmented outputs. In this work, we propose Hierarchical Step Decomposition (HSD), a training-free framework for online VSG that leverages the semantic understanding capabilities of Large Multimodal Models. HSD addresses two central challenges in online grounding: constructing semantically coherent temporal segments from a streaming video, and bridging the semantic gap between coarse procedural step descriptions and visual observations. To construct elementary temporal units, HSD incrementally groups incoming segments into semantically consistent events, using an anchor caption that is continuously validated against the visual stream. Based on these events, we perform zero-shot procedural step classification and selectively refine uncertain predictions by decomposing candidate steps into finegrained substeps that capture more nuanced visual evidence. By operating on semantically coherent events rather than every fixed-length segment, HSD reduces redundant computation and produces more stable predictions. Experiments on HT-Step, Ego4D Goal-Step, and CrossTask show that HSD substantially outperforms state-of-the-art methods, overall achieving better step recognition, more accurate temporal localization, and faster inference.

papers.title: Constructions of Variable Modified Chaplygin-Jacobi and Chaplygin-Abel Gases from Geometrothermodynamics
papers.abstract: Understanding the physical origin of the Universe's late-time accelerated expansion remains one of the central open problems in modern cosmology. Geometrothermodynamics (GTD) offers a compelling route to this problem, providing a geometric framework that unifies thermodynamics with contact and Riemannian geometry to encode the equilibrium properties of a physical system directly into its underlying geometric structure. In this work, we employ the GTD formalism to investigate cosmological models capable of explaining the observed accelerated expansion of the Universe. As an important outcome, our simple model exhibits dynamical behavior that provides a reasonable description of the late-time evolution of the Universe. We study the Chaplygin-Jacobi and Chaplygin-Abel gas models and their variable forms within geometrothermodynamics by deriving their thermodynamic relations, entropy, and equations of state. The free parameters of the models are constrained through a Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) analysis using several observational datasets, including cosmic chronometers combined with baryon acoustic oscillations (CC+BAO), DESI DR2 BAO data, DESI DR2 combined with the DES-SN5YR and Union3 Type Ia supernova compilations. The statistical performance of the models is assessed using the Akaike and Bayesian Information Criteria (AIC and BIC). We further examine their cosmological evolution through the deceleration parameter, the dark-energy equation-of-state parameter, and higher-order kinematic diagnostics, including the jerk and snap parameters. The perturbative stability of the models is also investigated through the squared sound speed.

papers.title: A Quantitative Interpretation of Useful Call-by-Value
papers.abstract: In this work, we present the first semantic interpretation of useful call-by-value evaluation through a non-idempotent intersection type system called U. One first contribution of this paper is a characterisation of termination of useful call-by-value evaluation via U-typability. That is, a term is typable in system U if and only if it terminates in the useful call-by-value strategy. As a second contribution, we show that system U provides a quantitative interpretation for useful call-by-value evaluation, offering exact step-count information for program evaluation. Even though the specification of the operational semantics of useful evaluation is highly complex, system U is notably simple. As far as we know, system U is one of the scarce quantitative type systems capturing exactly the substitution step-count for variables and abstractions in an open call-by-value strategy. Our third contribution is a termination-equivalence result between standard call-by-value, which may perform erasing reductions, and useful call-by-value, which is non-erasing. To establish this result, we introduce a non-erasing restriction of standard call-by-value, a refinement that serves as an intermediate calculus bridging standard and useful call-by-value. We show that all three calculi have the same termination behaviour, and hence induce the same observational equivalence.

papers.title: Reversible photorefractive attack in continuous-variable quantum key distribution
papers.abstract: Quantum key distribution (QKD) offers information-theoretic security, but device imperfections introduce implementation vulnerabilities. Experimental evidence of the security consequences of transmitter vulnerabilities in continuous-variable QKD (CV-QKD) remains limited. Here, we experimentally investigate a reversible photorefractive attack in a local-local-oscillator CV-QKD system. Moderate blue-light illumination reduces the modulation variance of a lithium-niobate IQ modulator to a stable value without appreciably increasing estimated excess noise. The variance recovers after illumination is removed. We elucidate the underlying physical mechanisms and develop an attack that exploits recovery to compromise modulation calibration. Receiver measurements confirm that the resulting calibration mismatch leads to overestimated channel transmittance and underestimated excess noise. Key rate calculations based on measured parameters yield a positive estimated rate when the correctly calibrated rate is nonpositive. Recovery can also make the preceding manipulation harder to identify through later inspection. This work provides the first system-level experimental evidence that a reversible photorefractive response can be exploited to compromise modulation calibration in CV-QKD. These findings highlight reversible changes in quantum transmitters as a practical security concern, motivating security analyses and protection strategies that account for both optical perturbations and subsequent recovery.

papers.title: $\mathcal{N}=4$ Super Yang-Mills Flux Tube in AdS
papers.abstract: We study a supersymmetric Wilson line on the boundary of $\mathcal{N}=4$ super Yang-Mills theory in AdS$_4$, or equivalently on a half-space, as a model for exploring the connection between holographic strings and confining flux tubes. The boundary breaks four-dimensional conformal symmetry and is expected to remove integrability, bringing this system closer to a confining string while preserving enough supersymmetry to constrain its dynamics. Working in the planar limit, we analyze the defect spectrum at weak and strong coupling and compute the superconformal index, thereby relating the perturbative gauge-theory description to the worldsheet excitations of a long holographic string. These complementary perspectives allow us to propose a map between operators in the two regimes, under which the worldsheet axion, in particular, becomes a two-particle state at strong coupling. The resulting picture supports a smooth interpolation from an exponentially growing gauge-theory spectrum to the Cardy-like spectrum of a string worldsheet, providing a non-integrable supersymmetric model for investigating the spectral reorganization expected in confining gauge theories.

papers.title: Cubic-Zn(1-x)Mn(x)Te optical modes across the phonon and phonon-polariton regimes
papers.abstract: Alloying offers a convenient route to tune the physical properties of semiconductors, at the price, however, of local lattice/bond distortions needed to accommodate the lattice mismatch. Being nearly lattice-matched and moreover highly resistant to lattice and bond distortions thanks to a largely covalent bonding, cubic Zn(1-x)Mn(x)Te sets a benchmark to test the sensitivity of lattice vibrations to minimum lattice and bond distortions induced by alloying. We explore experimentally the two transverse optical regimes of cubic Zn(1-x)Mn(x)Te (x<0.7), with ab initio calculations in support: (1) the phonon-polariton regime at quasi-infinite (photon-like) wavelengths averaging over the alloy disorder, probed by forward-Raman scattering, and (2) the purely-mechanical phonon regime down to minimum wavelengths nearly matching the lattice constant zooming into the alloy disorder, achieved by inelastic neutron scattering. The short Zn-Te bond is found to exhibit a compact optical duo distinguishing homo from hetero local bond environments (1 bond: 2 mode), as explained by the percolation model. This deviates from the historical Zn(1-x)Mn(x)Te MREI (modified-random-element-isodisplacement) scheme inspired from classical Raman and infrared studies, in which the optical modes are blind to the bond environment (1-bond: 1-mode). So, the test is positive, reinforcing the status of the percolation scheme as a robust decryptor of (even small) lattice distortions induced by alloying through the lattice dynamics.

papers.title: Inevitability of the Petz transpose map
papers.abstract: Bayes' rule is central to classical statistical inference: given a prior and a stochastic model, it determines the corresponding retrodictive conditional probabilities. In quantum theory, however, the question of whether an equally general rule of retrodiction exists and, if so, whether it is uniquely determined remains nontrivial. Here we prove that a retrodiction assignment defined for all priors and channels, which takes each predicted output state back to its prior, must coincide with the Petz transpose map if it is involutive, respects sequential and parallel composition, and agrees with unitary inversion. The theorem holds for channels between finite-dimensional full matrix algebras, with the input and output spaces restricted to the supports of the corresponding reference states. In particular, affinity under probabilistic mixtures and the characteristic square-root dependence on the reference states follow from these requirements rather than being postulated. Without involutivity, the remaining requirements characterize a family of doubly rotated Petz maps. Our result thus explains why the Petz transpose map arises in seemingly different areas of quantum theory: it is the unique quantum analogue of Bayes' rule compatible with these consistency requirements.

papers.title: Nonminimal Scalar-curvature Coupling Noncanonical Warm Inflation
papers.abstract: We investigate a noncanonical warm inflationary model with a nonminimal coupling between the inflaton field and scalar curvature. Within the Jordan frame, we derive the modified background equations and establish the slow-roll conditions through a linear stability analysis. We find that the nonminimal coupling enhances the effective damping and modifies the potential gradient, facilitating slow-roll evolution even for relatively steep potentials. Using the stochastic approach, we derive the Langevin equation for inflaton fluctuations and obtain the primordial scalar and tensor power spectra. Our results show that the scalar spectrum is nearly scale-invariant, while the combined effects of nonminimal coupling, noncanonical dynamics, and thermal dissipation can further suppress the tensor-to-scalar ratio. Moreover, the model can sustain warm inflation even in the weak-dissipation regime and accommodate sub-Planckian field excursions in suitable parameter regions. These findings highlight the potential of this framework as a viable extension of conventional warm inflation.

papers.title: FARE: Factor-Aware Retrieval with Error-Guided Fusion for Retail Forecasting
papers.abstract: Retail sales forecasting underpins inventory planning, yet promotions and calendar events reshape short-term demand. Although each factor usually has historical occurrences, the complete factor combination of a target week often has few precedents. The challenge is therefore to retrieve informative partial matches and weight them by their reliability, which varies across series. We propose FARE(Factor-Aware Retrieval with Error-Guided Fusion), which ranks historical weeks separately for each known target-week factor and merges the selected weeks into a factor reference under a fixed budget. Guided by shrunk errors from completed development weeks and the current disagreement among candidates, a first gate mixes this factor reference with a shape reference from similar sales histories, and a second gate controls how strongly the mixture corrects a backbone forecast. Both gates remain fixed during testing. On Favorita, M5, Rossmann, and Rohlik, FARE reduces the weighted absolute percentage error (WAPE) of five backbones by 11.46%, 4.06%, 14.63%, and 10.16% on average. With Chronos-2 frozen, FARE also outperforms conventional and existing enhancement methods, including supervised residual correction and retrieval augmentation. Code is available at https://github.com/HousonGu/FARE .

papers.title: A Negotiation-Aware Hybrid LLM Framework for Intent Interpretation and Service Discovery
papers.abstract: Increasingly, users express their needs as natural-language intents rather than structured requests. These intents may be incomplete, high-level, or internally conflicting. A conflicting intent either violates fundamental properties of the cloud paradigm or states mutually inconsistent requirements. Classical composition approaches are designed for structured, low-level, and complete requests. They cannot interpret such intents, discover suitable services from provider catalogs, or negotiate conflicting requirements with users. To address this gap, we propose a negotiation-aware framework for intent interpretation and service discovery. The framework first refines the natural-language intent and dynamically detects conflicts. It then structures the intent into a provider-independent TOSCA template. For each specification, it retrieves candidate service offers through deterministic matching grounded in cloud provider offerings. Some conflicts arise during interpretation. Other requirements prove unsatisfiable during discovery. Both are resolved through iterative natural-language negotiation with the user. We evaluate the framework on 70 diverse intents against single-shot and enhanced-prompting baselines. It improves recall and F1 for both conflict detection and service discovery. It also eliminates hallucinated offers and resolves conflicts at a cost proportional to their number.

papers.title: Fisher Contrastive Learning to Mitigate Feature Suppression: A Case Study in Acute Promyelocytic Leukemia Diagnosis
papers.abstract: Self-supervised contrastive learning (SSCL) learns representations by contrasting augmented views of the same sample, but it can exhibit feature suppression, where dominant or easy-to-learn factors suppress other class-relevant signals, degrading the performance of representations, particularly in high-dimensional data with heterogeneous features. We introduce Fisher Contrastive Learning (FCL), which uses a regularized Fisher trace criterion to address feature suppression. FCL learns embeddings by maximizing the discriminative strength of Fisher discriminant functions, producing representations that preserve class-relevant information implied by the augmentation process. We prove that the representations learned by FCL could alleviate the feature suppression effects. We demonstrate FCL on simulated benchmarks designed to induce feature suppression and on a real-world biomedical application, pretraining on large white blood cell microscopy image dataset and transfer learning for diagnosis of acute promyelocytic leukemia in an external cohort. In all experiments, FCL outperforms the self-supervised baselines and yields more robust and discriminative representations.

papers.title: Model-assisted estimation of the finite population mean via local linear regression with associated kernels
papers.abstract: In this paper, we propose a general regression-assisted estimator of the population mean based on local regression with associated kernels, a broad class that encompasses both classical (symmetric) kernels, such as the Gaussian and Epanechnikov kernels, and asymmetric kernels, such as the gamma kernel. We establish the asymptotic properties of the proposed estimator, including explicit expressions for the bias, mean squared error, and asymptotic normality, under a unified framework that applies to any kernel in this class. Through simulation studies on nonnegative data and one real-data application, we compare the finite-sample performance of the estimator based on the gamma kernel with those relying on the Gaussian and Epanechnikov kernels. When the data are supported on the positive real line, symmetric kernels suffer from boundary bias near zero due to mass assignment outside the support, whereas the gamma kernel, naturally adapted to $[0,\infty)$, alleviates this effect. The results confirm that the choice of kernel within the associated matters in practice, and that asymmetric kernels provide a reliable and efficient alternative when the underlying regression function is supported on the positive real line or exhibits marked asymmetry.

papers.title: Who Owns Digital News, and Who Gets Cited: Measuring Media Concentration Across 77 Countries and Seven AI Systems
papers.abstract: Digital news outlets compete for audience attention. Search engines equipped with generative AI systems such as Google's AI overviews increasingly decide where that attention goes, as well as the revenue it represents. Yet, the lack of a consistent data collection infrastructure between national-level regulatory bodies has hindered between-country comparative analysis of media concentration, and with it any assessment of how these intermediaries reshape digital news markets. To address this issue, we compile an ownership dataset for 9,761 digital news outlets drawn from Wikipedia and Wikidata, achieving high agreement with independently compiled US and UK news directories. Using this dataset, we derive traffic-weighted concentration indices for 77 countries. We find that journalists report more owner pressure in countries with higher concentration, and that outlet-level measures understate concentration, with owner-level indices a median 1.30x higher. Applying concentration measures to AI-mediated news discovery, we find that citation distributions from major AI systems are up to 2.08x more concentrated than traffic, and that if Google AI Overviews mediated all organic search, the resulting rise in US concentration would be several times that associated with highly regulated media mergers and acquisitions. Finally, our analyses indicate that AI systems preferentially cite state-controlled media outlets when prompted in that country's native language. Together, these findings raise concerns about the effect AI systems may have on digital media. We release the dataset to enable the monitoring of digital news globally, so that the impact of disruptive technologies on digital media markets can be tracked as they emerge.

papers.title: Closing the Log Gap: Minimax-Optimal Regret for Episodic RL
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study the regret minimization problem in episodic tabular MDPs. Our algorithm achieves the first expected regret bound scaling as $\sqrt{H^3 S A K}$ for sufficiently large $K$, where $H$ is the episode length, $K$ is the number of episodes, and $S$ and $A$ are the numbers of states and actions, respectively. Our method is the first to match the minimax lower bound \emph{without extra polylog factors}. We introduce a variant of UCBVI which does not maintain strictly optimistic estimates, and uses MOSS-style exploration bonuses whose logarithmic terms adapt to both visit counts and estimated variances. A key challenge is controlling the propagation of errors caused by under-optimism, which we accomplish in an occupancy-weighted way, avoiding logarithmic overhead that would be incurred by uniform-over-rows concentration. Our analysis develops time-uniform and variance-aware concentration bounds that may be of independent interest. As a corollary we also develop an algorithm for $(\varepsilon, δ)$-PAC best-policy identification, which is the first to match the $Ω\big(H^3 SA\log(\frac{1}δ)\varepsilon^{-2}\big)$ minimax lower bound up to constants in some regimes.

papers.title: EventSeeColor: Learning to Reconstruct Color from Monochrome Events
papers.abstract: Event cameras capture visual brightness changes under challenging lighting conditions. However, traditional event-based image reconstruction targets grayscale intensity and produces images without scene color. Color distinguishes surfaces with similar intensity. Reconstructing color from events can reveal appearance differences that reconstructed grayscale images cannot express. Although monochrome event cameras do not directly measure color, their event-triggering patterns depend on surface reflectance, illumination, and the sensor's spectral response. These patterns may contain cues that support color reconstruction. In this paper, we present EventSeeColor, which uses event-reconstructed grayscale and aligned events to jointly guide a diffusion colorizer. Grayscale-derived semantic context supports color inference, while region-balanced chroma supervision and local RGB refinement improve color distribution, brightness, and texture. In the combined evaluation on two real event datasets, EventSeeColor achieves the best structural similarity, learned perceptual scores, and chromatic-region color difference among the external methods.

papers.title: Beyond $χ^2$: Ensemble null tests for reliable scientific discovery
papers.abstract: Unrecognized systematic errors can survive standard checks and undermine scientific discoveries. Null tests and experimental controls can expose these failures, but averaging measurements or reducing them to scalar statistics can hide important structure. We propose ensemble null tests that compare multivariate distributions with references from observations or simulations. We demonstrate their benefits across science. In cosmic microwave background simulations, they detect systematic effects missed by conventional $χ^2$ tests. In Gaia data, they detect velocity asymmetry as sensitively as an informed search. In a CRISPR screen, they expose a control mismatch in DNA damage and reveal which cellular profiles drive it. As scientific datasets grow, ensemble testing turns repeated measurements into a broader search for unknown unknowns, strengthening the empirical foundation for scientific discovery.

papers.title: Optimal subtrees of finite metric graphs
papers.abstract: We consider a metric graph analog of a classical extremal problem for Riemann surfaces studied by Teichmüller, Jenkins, Strebel, and others. In particular, we prove that on any finite metric graph with a marked point, there is a unique open subtree which maximizes a metric graph analog of the reduced modulus, and we also give an equivalent characterization of this optimal subtree in terms of balanced harmonic measures.

papers.title: Retrieval Sequencing in a Compact Storage System with Side Access
papers.abstract: In a compact storage system with side access, bins are arranged in adjacent vertical stacks. In each retrieval cycle, bins blocking access are lifted to create a temporary tunnel through which a robot extracts one requested bin from the side. The lifted bins are then lowered again, and the energy expenditure of the cycle equals the number of lifted bins. Given a pick list known in advance, we seek a retrieval order that minimizes total energy expenditure. For every number of stacks, we prove that the total energy separates into an instance constant and a pairwise penalty, and that every energy-optimal order is laminar within each stack. For two stacks, we prove that the retrieval sequencing problem is solvable in polynomial time. For three stacks, we give an exact polynomial-time reduction to a merge problem and characterize which merge-problem instances arise from the storage model. We define a recursive class of retrieval orders and construct a polynomial-time dynamic program that minimizes energy expenditure over this class. Finally, we quantify the additional energy savings from batching, which allows several requested bins to be retrieved in one cycle.

papers.title: Coexistence of Superconductivity and Chern insulators with |C| $\geq 1$ in twisted rhombohedral bilayer-trilayer graphene
papers.abstract: Rhombohedral multilayer graphene (RMG) has been demonstrated as a promising platform for investigating strongly correlated phases of matter. Here, we observe a coexistence of superconductivity and Chern insulators in a twisted rhombohedral bilayer-trilayer graphene moiré superlattice. Superconductivity, evidenced by a sharp transition with a critical temperature of ~180 mK, nonlinear I-V with a BKT temperature of 135 mK, and a signature of phase-sensitive interference patterns, emerges from a symmetry-breaking Fermi surface near v = -2 and D = 0, and it survives at a large in-plane magnetic field up to 2 T, strongly deviating from the Pauli limit. Moreover, we observe a strong modulation of the Ginzburg-Landau coherence length from 467 nm to 145 nm as the in-plane magnetic field increases from 0 to 2 T, whereas the critical current Ic barely changes. Unlike previous studies in RMG, we observe a competition between superconductivity and a correlated insulator at v = -2, monitored by displacement fields and twist angles. Note that we also observe integer Chern insulators with C = 1, 3, and -3 at v = 1/2, 1, and 3, respectively, for large D > 0 in the same superconducting device. The observations establish twisted rhombohedral graphene multilayers as a fascinating system to investigate unconventional superconductivity, high Chern number topology, and their interplay.

papers.title: Temporal equivalent of the Sommerfeld half-plane problem
papers.abstract: Sommerfeld's half-plane problem, describing diffraction of a monochromatic wave by a semi-infinite perfectly electric conducting (PEC) infinitesimally thin plate, is one of the cornerstones of classical electromagnetic scattering theory. Here we study its temporal analogue: a semi-infinite medium with the Drude dispersion, adjacent to air, whose plasma frequency is rapidly reduced to zero, thus turning it into air, while a monochromatic wave with frequency below the plasma frequency illuminates it under normal incidence. Unlike the PEC plate, the Drude medium supports evanescent penetration of the field prior to its temporal transition; the temporal interface here acts as the analogue of the sharp spatial boundary in the Sommerfeld problem, but now separates two time intervals rather than two spatial half-planes. We show that this transition forces the standing wave in air in front of the Drude medium and the evanescent fields inside it to propagate in both directions, while preserving their spatial field structure. In addition, we observe the excitation of additional electric and magnetic field waves generated by a "DC" current density associated with the time interface. Our findings offer insight into the electromagnetic wave behavior at temporal transitions in dispersive media and may find applications in time- and space-time metamaterials

papers.title: Measuring Organizational Influence on Digital News: An Information-Theoretic Framework for Media Pluralism and Editorial Independence
papers.abstract: News consolidation is accelerating, yet regulators have no measurement frameworks for determining whether owners shape editorial decisions. Existing evidence comes from single cases, where pluralism and independence are measured separately, if at all. We ask whether ownership impacts editorial decisions across the digital news ecosystem, and if so, how acquisitions affect this. We derive editorial independence and internal pluralism using partial information decomposition, which separates news coverage overlap with sister outlets from coverage overlap with all outlets. Using public datasets, we apply our measures monthly from 2018 to 2026 to 1,364 US news websites on three editorial decisions: which events they cover, which sources they link to, and what they put on their front pages. We find that co-owned outlets share up to 40 times more information about these decisions than expected by chance. Ownership accounts for far more variation in independence than network affiliation does and, upon being acquired, outlets lose independence sooner than matched controls, quickly converging on their new owner. In broadcast news, by comparison, we find that it is network affiliation, not ownership, that accounts for more content overlap. Finally, we discuss policy implications and suggest that media regulators have blocked large deals rather than editorially detrimental ones. We hope that this work can serve as a framework for comparative media analyses going forward.

papers.title: Thermal Stability and Structural Relaxation Kinetics of Commercially Pure Titanium
papers.abstract: This work explores the structural relaxation of cryorolled commercially pure titanium subjected to subsequent annealing.Nanostructured specimens with an average grain size of ~50 nm were produced by plastic deformation via cryogenic rolling at 100 K to a true strain of 1.20, followed by annealing at 425 K, 525 K, 725 K, and 945 K. Microstructural evolution was examined using electron microscopy and X-ray diffraction. Cryogenic rolling was found to induce pronounced grain fragmentation, with coherent scattering regions (CSRs) of 30-50 nm dominating the substructure. X-ray diffraction analysis revealed that annealing drives crystallite growth: a slight increase at 525 K, accelerated coarsening at 725 K, and complete recrystallization at 945 K. The kinetics of grain growth follow the classical Lifshitz-Slyozov-Wagner model, with a growth exponent of ~4, reflecting the role of triple junctions and defect-controlled boundary diffusion. The activation energy, estimated at ~97 kJ/mol, corresponds to typical values for grain boundary diffusion in α-Ti, confirming that cryogenic deformation produces a highly non-equilibrium microstructure whose relaxation is strongly temperature dependent.

papers.title: Comments on $\bf{η'}$ nuclei and on the $Λ$ binding energy of the hypertriton
papers.abstract: I briefly discuss two apparent puzzles: (i) is the observation of $η'$(958) bound states in $^{11}$C at GSI [1] compatible with a nearly vanishing real part of $η'N$ scattering length [2]? and (ii) is the $Λ$ binding energy of the hypertriton (${{_Λ}^3}$H), the lightest particle-stable hypernucleus, very small (63$^{+38}_{-31}$ keV, J-PARC E73 [3]) or very large (523$\pm$76 keV, MAMI [4])? Here, I suggest that MAMI's observed weak-decay pion momentum peak originates from ${{_Λ}^7}$He, not from ${{_Λ}^3}$H \cite{Gal26}.

papers.title: A density calculus for quantum field theory
papers.abstract: These notes provide an introduction to Haagerup noncommutative $L^p$ spaces for quantum field theorists. The aim is to explain how the familiar calculus of density matrices, fractional powers, and Schatten norms extends to local observable algebras of type~III, where an intrinsic trace is unavailable. We develop the construction first for a matrix algebra, making the crossed product, its trace, and the dual action explicit, before passing to general von Neumann algebras. Particular attention is paid to the representation of normal states by Haagerup densities and to the distinction between the crossed-product trace and the canonical Haagerup functional used to compute expectation values. As a concrete application, we calculate the sandwiched Rényi divergence for a coherent excitation of a chiral current, verifying monotonicity under restriction and the Rényi quantum null energy condition at every real order $α>1$. The presentation assumes familiarity with quantum mechanics and elementary quantum field theory, while introducing the operator-algebraic concepts needed for the construction and calculation.

papers.title: Beyond CCT: Multi-channel SPD recovery for per-shot camera color correction
papers.abstract: Modern cameras correct color via two or three pre-calibrated 3x3 matrices interpolated by Correlated Color Temperature (CCT). This collapses the illuminant SPD to a scalar. LEDs, fluorescents, and mixed sources sit off the Planckian locus, and metameric illuminants with the same chromaticity demand different optimal CCMs that a CCT pipeline cannot distinguish. We recover the illuminant SPD instead using non-negative least squares against a basis dictionary, conditioned on the camera white point and a multi-channel ambient-light sensor (ALS). A closed-form 3x3 CCM is then fit per shot. On a synthetic benchmark of 300 illuminants and 3,100 reflectances, mean angular error drops from 1.89 to 1.20 degrees, with a 1.7x tail reduction on the LED-like off-Planckian group (n=45) where metameric ambiguity is tangible. The gain holds under realistic ALS imperfections and observation noise, and the same off-Planckian advantage carries over to 1,684 real measured SPDs.

papers.title: Cage-related crystal-field effects in the paramagnetic range of PrB$_6$
papers.abstract: New insights into the paramagnetic range of PrB$_6$ below 50 K are revealed through specific-heat, thermal-expansion and magnetic measurements. The latent heats of the two successive magnetic transitions, together with an improved description of the lattice contribution, enable a detailed determination of the thermal variation of the magnetic entropy. Immediately above the first-order magnetic ordering temperature ($T_N = 6.7$ K), the magnetic entropy per Pr$^{3+}$ is close to that of a doublet, instead of the triplet crystal-field ground state identified by inelastic neutron scattering. Temperatures in excess of 30 K are required to reach the entropy of the threefold-degenerate ground state. This is reminiscent of the CeB$_6$ case and, similarly, strongly suggests a dynamical splitting of the crystal-field ground state within the boron cage. Further evidence of this splitting is provided by the analysis of the low-temperature paramagnetic susceptibility, which resembles that of a non-magnetic ground state. In addition, a large thermal-expansion anomaly is observed below 20 K, consistent with the expected centrifugal Jahn-Teller effect.

papers.title: Multivariate Lebesgue bounds for R-Leja lower grids
papers.abstract: We establish an algebraic upper bound for the Lebesgue constant of multivariate polynomial interpolation on $\mathfrak R$-Leja lower grids. For each fixed dimension $d\geq2$ and every nonempty finite lower set $A\subset\mathbb N_0^d$, let $P_A$ denote the corresponding grid with $N=|A|$ nodes. We prove $Λ(P_A)\leq C_dN^{β_d}$, where $q_d=d/(d-1)$ and $β_d=1+q_d^{-1}\log_2(1+2^{q_d})$. The exponent satisfies $β_2=2.160964\ldots$ and increases to $\log_2 6=2.584962\ldots$ as $d\to\infty$, improving both the cubic estimate and the exponent $3-1/d$ obtained from quadratic prefix bounds. Our proof exploits the binary structure of known univariate estimates to control sums of powers of Lebesgue constants over interpolation prefixes. A weighted Hölder inequality and a disjoint-box packing argument then transfer these prefix-moment bounds to arbitrary lower sets. The resulting estimate is uniform over all lower-set shapes and choices of disk Leja maximizers, with constants depending only on $d$.

papers.title: Control of Seizure Dynamics in a Bistable System with Pulsatile Inputs
papers.abstract: Bistable neural population models describe transitions associated with epilepsy through the coexistence of a stable equilibrium representing normal neural activity and a stable limit cycle representing seizure-like oscillations. Perturbations that drive the system outside the equilibrium's basin of attraction can trigger transitions to seizure-like activity. Enlarging this basin enables the system to recover normal activity from a larger set of perturbed states, providing a model-based mechanism for reducing frequency of seizure initiation. Motivated by electrical brain stimulation, this paper investigates basin enlargement using pulsatile feedback control. Combining higher-order averaging with periodic near-identity transformations, we establish conditions under which nonzero-mean and zero-mean pulsatile feedback gains enlarge the basin of attraction and derive guidelines for pulse design. Numerical simulations validate the theoretical enlargement.

papers.title: Rotation overcharges vectorized black holes
papers.abstract: A charged black hole has a ceiling: extremality bounds the charge that a given mass and spin can support. Vector hair has so far only lowered it. In the Einstein--Maxwell--Vector (EMV) model, where a massless vector field couples nonminimally to the electromagnetic invariant, the spherically symmetric vectorized Reissner--Nordström black holes are strictly undercharged: vector hair is paid for in charge. Whether this ceiling is a property of the vector field or merely of spherical symmetry has remained open, because spherical symmetry hides the hair's mass as well: its Komar mass vanishes identically and the exact identity $M_V=2Ω_HJ_V$ degenerates to $0=0$. Rotation lifts both degeneracies at once. We construct the rotating solutions of the model, the first in this setting, and find that the hair's mass is not a free parameter but a second-order invariant of the rotational response, fixed by $M_V=2Ω_HJ_V$. Above a coupling threshold the ceiling gives way: the domain of existence crosses the extremal Kerr--Newman bound, reaching $q=Q/M>1$ with $q^2+χ^2$ up to $1.84$, while at $α=5$ the maximum charge stays below it. The shadow is where the hair becomes visible. At $(q,χ)=(0.9947,0.10)$, near the extremal bound, the hair contributes an ellipticity of $8.30\%$, against $0.44\%$ from the charge and $0.06\%$ from rotation --- a factor of $19$ that charging a Kerr black hole cannot mimic; at the overcharged solution $(q,χ)=(1.2527,0.10)$ the total ellipticity reaches $25.6\%$. Whether the branch is ghost-free remains open, but the existing no-go criteria do not settle it: they assume a background and a dispersion relation that do not hold here.

papers.title: Polarimetric Low-Rank Imaging of Anisotropic Maxwell Media
papers.abstract: We consider three-dimensional imaging of compactly supported anisotropic electric media from fixed-frequency polarimetric Maxwell far-field data. Maxwell transversality creates an obstruction absent from scalar Born inversion: each measurement determines only a projected action of the tensor-valued Fourier transform. We first resolve this obstruction by a finite-dimensional polarimetric inversion. For a general complex $3\times3$ contrast, three incidence--observation configurations are necessary, and we give an explicit three-configuration design that is sufficient at every nonzero interior Fourier point. Its Gram determinant yields quantitative conditioning information and exhibits the loss of recoverability at the boundary of the accessible Fourier ball. After tensor demixing, the inverse problem reduces componentwise to restricted Fourier inversion on the unit ball, which we regularize by spectral cutoff in three-dimensional ball generalized prolate spheroidal wave functions. For discrete acquisition, a combined reconstruction error estimate separates the effects of measurement noise, polarimetric amplification, off-grid Fourier mismatch, quadrature error, Born modeling error, and spectral truncation. Numerical tests examine polarimetric conditioning and use analytically generated Born data to compare three- and six-configuration recovery and assess off-grid sensitivity. Reconstructions from full-Maxwell volume-integral data assess the effects of noise, wavenumber, and basis choice, as well as the recovery of different tensor components.

papers.title: Gravitational waves away from a Schwarzschild black hole: full spectrum analysis
papers.abstract: Gravitational waves as one approaches Schwarzschild null infinity are the core of our investigation, treated as the spin-weighted generalisation of a massless scalar field. In particular, we compute their full spectrum, consistent with observations coming from LIGO and VIRGO experiments. This paper continues recent work by the authors, where the Poincaré asymptotic expansion was exploited in black hole perturbation theory. The mathematical formalism we developed is now intimately connected with gravitational wave phenomenology, providing new mathematical tools to investigate their features.

papers.title: Hidden Disparities in Ranking: Category-Aware Fairness via Distributional Stability
papers.abstract: We study the problem of fair ranking in recommender systems. We provide a formal probabilistic framework in which ranking policies are distributions over permutations, and the utility of a user is the exposure given to the items they interact with, relative to that of an ideal ranking. We consider utility parity across user groups, as well as its category-aware refinement, conditional utility parity, which requires parity within each category of items. Following a recent view of fairness as distributional stability, we show that both criteria are equivalent to the stability of the utility under changes in the composition of user groups. Optimizing over mixtures of ranking policies leads to a second-order cone program, for which we provide generalization bounds. A numerical study validates our theoretical findings.

papers.title: Linking-form splitting and four-dimensional genera of knots
papers.abstract: By Gilmer's splitting lemma, the linking form of a rational homology sphere that bounds a 4-manifold is the orthogonal sum of a metabolic summand and a summand presented by a form of the rank of the intersection form. The lemma underlies Gilmer's slice genus theorem and the rank criteria of Murakami-Yasuhara and Gilmer-Livingston for nonorientable surfaces and the 4-dimensional clasp number. We show that the lemma and these results, as stated, are false. For each prime $p \equiv 3 \pmod 8$ we construct knots bounding smooth Möbius bands, and knots bounding smooth punctured tori with clasp number one, whose linking forms have no such summand of rank at most two. We then determine what remains true: the lemma holds up to Witt equivalence and for cube-free orders, and its conclusions about summands hold away from exceptional primes and for orientable surfaces of genus at least two. Finally, we find the optimal Witt-class bound for the topological nonorientable 4-genus.

papers.title: Uniform duplication-divergence random graphs I: Degrees and Local Limits
papers.abstract: We study a growing random graph in which each new vertex chooses a uniformly random parent, joins that parent with probability $r\in(0,1]$, and independently joins each of the parent's current neighbors with probability $p\in(0,1)$. Let $p_c$ be the unique solution of $p_c e^{p_c}=1$. For $0<p<p_c$, we prove that the empirical degree distribution converges in probability to the stationary distribution $π$ of an explicit reset-and-growth Markov chain. Its upper tail satisfies $π((y,\infty))\sim C_{p,r}y^{-κ}$, where $C_{p,r}>0$ and $κ>0$ solves $p^κ+pκ=1$. This confirms predictions from physics (Lambiotte, Krapivsky, Bhat and Redner, \textit{Physical Review Letters}, 2016). We further show that for every fixed radius $\ell$ and $p<p_c$, the empirical distribution of induced rooted $\ell$-neighborhoods converges to the invariant law of a graph-valued reset-and-growth Markov process. We give an explicit construction of the limiting graph using a marked ancestral genealogy. Its root component is almost surely finite for $r<1$, and infinite with exactly one end for $r=1$. Moreover, for every $0<p<1$, both the fixed-vertex degrees and the maximum degree grow on the scale $t^p$, and the vertex of maximum degree is eventually unique and persistent.

papers.title: Temporal regularization of petal modes in SCAO systems: The Soft-Limiter approach
papers.abstract: Extremely large telescopes (ELTs) rely on segmented mirrors and thick support structures that fragment the pupil. In single-conjugate AO (SCAO), this produces differential pistons, or petal modes. The Pyramid Wavefront Sensor (PWFS), baseline for ANDES, MICADO, HARMONI, and GMT-NGSAO, has poor sensitivity to these modes in the visible under realistic residual turbulence. We aim to prevent the "Island Effect", where poorly observed differential pistons accumulate and degrade the PSF, without compromising continuous-mode correction. We propose the Minimum Mean Square Error (MMSE) Soft-Limiter, a deterministic, lightweight controller combining a subspace MMSE estimator derived from von Kármán priors with a continuous temporal regularization. It acts as a leaky integrator applied only to the relative petal degrees of freedom. End-to-end SPECULA simulations of ELT/ANDES show that, while a classical integrator loses lock and wanders across multiple fringes at seeing $\ge 1.0''$, the MMSE Soft-Limiter confines the differential piston within a single fringe over the $0.6-1.2''$ range. It bounds the petal excursion and its science-band impact under severe turbulence, while keeping optimal continuous-mode correction at good seeing, without the Strehl penalty of spatial mitigation such as Edge Actuator Coupling. We derive and verify the operating window for the leakage gain, $g \lesssim g_{\mathrm{eff}}/π$: below it, the fast loop retains genuine physical steps up to $λ_{WFS}/2$ with a small droop. This maintains a stable modulo-$λ_{WFS}$ wavefront on the fast sensor, letting a slower phasing sensor resolve integer ambiguities. As the window narrows with turbulence, its boundaries cross near $1.0''$ seeing; beyond this, retaining physical discontinuities becomes the sole responsibility of the phasing channel, a key design driver for segmented ELTs.

papers.title: Von Neumann regular and semisimple rings realized as principal quotients of domains
papers.abstract: In this paper, we show that every commutative von Neumann regular ring is a quotient of a characteristic-zero Bézout domain by its principal Jacobson radical. We then characterize the commutative semisimple rings that occur as quotients of Dedekind domains. For a finite product of fields $R=\prod_{i=1}^n k_i$, such a presentation exists exactly when the cardinals $|k_i|^{\aleph_0}$ are all equal. When this condition holds, the source may be taken to be a characteristic-zero semilocal principal ideal domain, and the quotient ideal may again be its Jacobson radical.

papers.title: Locating and Closing Information Gaps in Multi-Agent Systems
papers.abstract: Multi-step Web tasks often require several LLM agents to gather and combine evidence. The communication graph of a fixed workflow restricts which agents can read each other's outputs: evidence retrieved by one agent may never reach the agent that needs it, leaving an information gap and an incomplete or incorrect answer. Adding a connection can deliver the missing evidence, but can also lead the receiver to adopt an incorrect upstream conclusion that displaces a correct answer; the final output alone does not separate the two. We propose Selective Probing and Link Insertion for Closing information gaps in multi-agent Execution (SPLICE), which locates information gaps per query and decides what to adopt after adding an edge. After the original workflow runs, SPLICE uses the query and node outputs to locate a possible gap, adds one directed edge from a source to a receiver to deliver the relevant evidence, and re-executes the receiver and affected downstream nodes, producing a candidate answer. The adoption decision reads both the final answers of the two runs and the process changes the edit caused inside the workflow: how far the receiver moved, where its new content came from, and whether the change reached the final answer. A selector trained on these process features chooses between adopting the candidate answer and retaining the original. On five benchmarks, SPLICE raises the task score on Web tool use by 8.0% and the mean score on four reasoning and planning benchmarks by 5.7% relative to the static skeleton, at 1.25 to 1.44$\times$ the skeleton's cost, and transfers zero-shot to four unseen backbones.

papers.title: Model-Based Retrieval of Four Years of JWST/NIRCam Wavefronts
papers.abstract: The fidelity of data recovered by the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) depends on precise monitoring of the mirror segments' surfaces and alignment. To this end, every few days the observatory takes pairs of defocused images of a reference star with its NIRCam instrument; a closed-source phase retrieval package is then employed to infer the wavefront. We here present camino (Computational Aberration Modelling and Inference for NIRCam Observations), an open-source algorithm to model NIRCam built in JAX using the differentiable Fresnel optics code dLUX and regularised maximum likelihood inference that has been conditioned on the entire archive of NIRCam wavefront sensing data. We typically improve the reduced chi-squared in fits to the defocused data from 60-65 to 12-13. We reconstruct the wavefront history of JWST from the beginning of science operations to early 2026. This open source implementation operates in parallel to the current STScI phase retrieval algorithm, allowing access by the broader scientific community to high-accuracy wavefront estimation and enabling its direct integration into science-analysis workflows. This represents a major step towards the ultimate goal of predictive calibration methods based on physics-based forward modelling, obviating the need for time-consuming observation of contemporaneous dedicated reference stars.

papers.title: Understanding axial attention in TSFMs through single location regression
papers.abstract: Recent advances in Time Series Foundation Models (TSFMs) increasingly rely on axial attention mechanisms, but despite their empirical success, the theoretical properties of axial attention remain largely unexplored. To bridge this gap, we extend the Single Location Regression framework introduced in Marion et al. [2025] to 2D structured data, in order to study sparse information settings where a target depends on a small number of tokens. We formulate an analytically tractable axial attention-type predictor and rigorously analyze its statistical properties and training dynamics. We prove that under a specific asymptotic regime and with knowledge of the underlying oracle parameters, our predictor achieves Bayes optimality, whereas a class of semi-linear simplifications strictly fails to do so, underlining the role of the inner non-linearity. We prove that for a specific temperature scaling, Projected Gradient Descent converges globally to the optimal oracle parameters. Extensive numerical experiments validate our theoretical findings and highlight the critical role of inverse temperature scheduling in empirical convergence.

papers.title: {DEMAND}: {A}n organic glass scintillator array for direct measurements of $(α,n)$ and $(p,n)$ reactions in inverse kinematics
papers.abstract: We have developed an array of up to 20 organic glass scintillator detectors, each consisting of a $3~\mathrm{cm}\times3~\mathrm{cm}\times3~\mathrm{cm}$ scintillator cube coupled to a photomultiplier tube. Sensitive to neutrons from a few hundred keV to several tens of MeV, the array was designed for use with recoil separators in inverse-kinematics measurements of astrophysical $(α,n)$ and $(p,n)$ reactions. It provides a prompt start signal for identifying recoil-neutron coincidences from the recoil time of flight. We characterize eight detectors used in an inverse-kinematics measurement of $^{22}\mathrm{Ne}(α,n)^{25}\mathrm{Mg}$, using source and in-beam data. From the widths of $γ$-ray Compton-edge peaks at 311, 341, 477, and 1062 keVee, we find an energy resolution described by $\mathrm{FWHM}(E)/E=\sqrt{A^2/E+B^2/E^2+C^2}$, with $A=0.00(7)$, $B=0.0618(54)$, and $C=0.135(5)$. The time-difference spectrum of nearest-neighbor $γ$-$γ$ coincidences from a $^{22}\mathrm{Na}$ source (250--600 keVee) gives a FWHM coincidence timing resolution of $910(40)$ ps, corresponding to a single-detector resolution of $640(30)$ ps. Mixed neutron-$γ$ fields from the in-beam reaction and a $^{241}\mathrm{AmBe}$ source show pulse-shape discrimination with an $n$-$γ$ figure of merit $>1$ down to about 100 keVee. Below 100 keVee, the total neutron yield can still be extracted using two-Gaussian fits to energy-gated pulse-shape discrimination spectra. Monte Carlo simulations of the present $^{22}\mathrm{Ne}(α,n)^{25}\mathrm{Mg}$ measurement give a neutron singles detection efficiency of $1.56(45)%$, with uncertainty dominated by systematic effects in the simulation inputs.

papers.title: AdMuse: Skill-Guided Creative Advertising Image Generation
papers.abstract: An outstanding creative advertising image should both attract attention and communicate a product's positioning. How to choose a persuasive conceptual bridge before rendering begins is challenging for advertising generation. We present AdMuse, a skill-guided multi-agent framework that distills high-quality advertisements into reusable creative skills for cross-domain advertising strategy. Rather than retrieving isolated exemplars, AdMuse abstracts recurring bridge patterns into a skill library that can guide new product briefs. At generation time, AdMuse coordinates skill routing, multi-candidate ideation and selection, and VLM-guided visual refinement: diverse skills propose alternative concepts, relative judgment selects the most promising direction, and vision-language feedback helps realize the selected intent in the final image. This design treats advertising creativity as a structured decision process rather than a single prompt-writing step. Experiments across diverse product and brand positionings show that AdMuse produces visually compelling advertisements that faithfully communicate product positioning.

papers.title: Video Generation Meets Agent Harness: Agentic Video Generation, Agentic World Modeling and Recursive Self-Improvement
papers.abstract: Video generation is shifting from end-to-end synthesis toward agentic generation, where planning, tool use, and feedback enable coherent, controllable multi-shot videos. In parallel, video world models provide action-conditioned observations and predicted futures, serving as interactive environments for agents. We study their intersection through the agent harness: an executable runtime that constructs context, exposes tools, maintains state, routes feedback, and manages budgets around video models. This report examines three directions. First, agentic video generation, where harnesses coordinate scripting, shot planning, asset management, production, and editing, alongside the evaluation challenges of these systems. Second, agentic world modeling, where harnesses mediate observation, control, execution, and state. We discuss hybrid designs in which game engines or agent-written programs maintain world state while video models render observations, and how agents and world models can mutually evaluate and improve one another. Third, recursive self-improvement (RSI) in video model development, distinguishing output revisions, updates to harness state, generator parameters, and evaluators, and changes to the improvement procedure itself. We identify how these improvements feed back into subsequent development. Across these directions, we analyze essential agent capabilities, including audiovisual perception, long-horizon planning, memory, code-based interaction, feedback-guided control, skill reuse, and multi-agent coordination. We conclude with challenges in autonomous video production, lifelong memory, programmable hybrid control, autonomous model development, provenance, cost accounting, and evaluation linking video quality and task performance to sustained improvements in models and harnesses.

papers.title: Bridging Semantics and Structure: A Theoretically Grounded Framework for Link Prediction on TAGs
papers.abstract: Link prediction on text-attributed graphs (TAGs) is a fundamental problem with applications in knowledge discovery, recommendation and beyond. Recent progress has highlighted the promise of combining Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) with Language Models (LMs) in order to leverage the complementary structural and semantic signals. However, due to the distinct inductive biases of GNNs and LMs, the design of an optimal fusion strategy remains an open research question. In this work, we present Bridge-LP, an intuitive, simple, efficient and theoretically grounded framework that unifies graph and language representations. It is built around three theoretically-justified design components: (D1) jumping connection of textual proximity, which enables robust LM training; (D2) compressed embedding, which encodes neighborhood information long exploited by classical link prediction heuristics, thereby enriching structural signals in a learnable way; and (D3) cache embedding training strategy, which reduces computational complexity. Together, these mechanisms establish an end-to-end cross-modal framework that scales to large graphs while capturing richer graph-text interactions. We conduct an extensive empirical evaluation, comparing against 40 existing models across 9 diverse datasets. Experiments show that Bridge-LP consistently outperforms state-of-the-art approaches, delivering up to a 43.06% improvement in Mean Reciprocal Rank (MRR) and setting a new benchmark for language-graph integration.

papers.title: Homogeneity Pursuit of Panel Data with Sparsity
papers.abstract: In panel data analysis, studying individual attributes is important for both methodological development and practical applications. Homogeneity in individual attributes and sparsity in coefficients are therefore important topics, as they help uncover relationships among individuals and identify the truly relevant covariates. However, many existing approaches do not explicitly exploit the potential grouping information contained in separately fitted individual-level penalized estimators to identify latent groups. To address this gap, we propose a hierarchical group recovery approach based on sparse initial estimation to jointly identify latent groups and sparse parameter structures in panel data. We first introduce a basic version that can efficiently identify homogeneity and sparsity. Based on this basic version, we further introduce a local search step to improve the performance of our method. Compared with existing methods, our approach shows the best overall performance when jointly considering estimation accuracy and computational efficiency. The simulation results demonstrate the effectiveness and advantages of our approach over existing approaches. We further apply the proposed approach to a real dataset to show its practical applicability.

papers.title: Apriel Voice 27B Preview: An Open Model for Speech, Reasoning, and Tool Use
papers.abstract: A capable voice assistant must do more than recognize words; it must understand requests, reason over context, sustain conversations, and act through tools. We present Apriel Voice 27B Preview, an open speech-language model that unifies these capabilities within a shared reasoning backbone while retaining text and image input modalities. Built on the post-trained Gemma 4 26B-A4B checkpoint, Apriel Voice directly processes speech and generates both responses and tool calls without requiring a separate dialogue model. We introduce a two-stage training procedure to adapt the model to speech. The first stage establishes the speech interface, while the second jointly adapts the projector and backbone through supervised fine-tuning, text replay, and source-dependent cross-entropy and forward Kullback--Leibler divergence supervision. Automatically constructed speech-conditioned dialogues provide conversational training data, while local teacher serving, overlapping teacher and student computation, and fused full-vocabulary losses enable efficient online distillation. In thinking mode, Apriel Voice achieves a score of 98.90 on Big Bench Audio, 81.13 on Speech-BFCL, and a task success rate of 65.51% on $τ$-Voice, with a mean latency of 1.91 seconds. It also achieves 51.27% English EVA accuracy and 74.13% experience pass@1. Finally, we deploy Apriel Voice 27B Preview on a custom serving platform to support interactive voice interactions.

papers.title: Optical Calibration of a Frequency-Domain-Multiplexed X-Ray TES Microcalorimeter Array via Photon-Number-Resolved Statistics
papers.abstract: Transition-edge sensor (TES) microcalorimeters for future X-ray space observatories require accurate low-energy calibration, a regime where conventional X-ray sources are limited by intrinsic linewidth, count rate, or experimental complexity. In this work, we investigate fibercoupled optical photons as a compact calibration tool for an Athena-like TES array. Optical pulses at 405 nm were generated with an acousto-optic modulator and delivered through an optical fiber onto a selected TES pixel inside a dilution refrigerator, via a dedicated cryogenic alignment interface. Externally triggered pulses were processed with an optimal-filter pipeline, including baseline subtraction, drift correction, and multi-Gaussian reconstruction of the pulse-height spectrum. The reconstructed spectra show resolved photon-number peaks consistent with the Poissonian statistics expected from an attenuated coherent source, reaching equivalent energies above 400 eV with a mean photon number exceeding 100 per pulse. The detector response was further tested for linearity by comparing the measured photon-number distributions against those predicted from the independently calibrated number of photons sent to the detector and a single, globally estimated detection efficiency, confirming Poissonian, linear behaviour across nearly two orders of magnitude in photon number. These results demonstrate that fiber-delivered optical photons can probe the few-eV to sub-keV response of Athena-like TES microcalorimeters, offering a practical and extensible framework for future low-energy calibration studies.

papers.title: New hierarchical matrices for fast kernel matrix-vector products with Applications to Gaussian processes and kernel ridge regression
papers.abstract: This article presents two new multilevel hierarchical matrices to perform fast kernel matrix-vector products in $d$ dimensions $(d>1)$, namely $\mathcal{H}_{hw}^{\prime}$, $\mathcal{H}_{hw}^{\prime \prime}$. We introduce a novel hybrid weak admissibility condition to construct these hierarchical matrices. More precisely, at coarser levels of the tree (i.e., larger blocks), we use a weak admissibility condition, wherein \textbf{far-field} and \textbf{vertex-sharing} clusters are considered admissible, while at the finer levels (i.e., smaller blocks), the \textbf{adjacent} clusters are treated as admissible. The admissible blocks at coarser levels of $\mathcal{H}_{hw}^{\prime}$ and $\mathcal{H}_{hw}^{\prime \prime}$ are represented using semi-nested and fully nested bases, respectively. In both hierarchical matrices, the finer levels at which adjacent clusters are treated as admissible are constructed in a non-nested fashion.
