Light-weight BEV forecasters meet latency requirements but often blur or suppress fast-moving actors at longer horizons. We present UFMF (Ultra-Fast Multi-modal Forecaster), a real-time forecaster that keeps an attention-free diagonal state-space temporal core while injecting targeted kinematic and geometric structure where lightweight models typically fail. A radar-guided velocity-aware dynamic prior (VADP) decomposes future displacement into a linear extrapolation plus a learned horizon-dependent residual. The resulting per-cell flow fields transport a compact dynamic latent subspace during rollout. Two auxiliary training constraints complement this branch: world-frame dynamic supervision enforces inter-horizon trajectory coherence, and class-conditioned vertical-profile supervision regularizes BEV-to-3D lifting. UFMF operates at 122 FPS on a single RTX 4090 and reaches 0.45 fast-displacement mIoU on nuScenes, outperforming recent occupancy world models at a fraction of their computational cost.

papers.title: Temporal and spatial couplings in the dynamics of human walking and running
papers.abstract: Rhythmic behaviours such as walking and running are commonly modelled as dynamical systems around a stable limit cycle. To keep such models tractable, it is usually assumed that each step depends only on the previous one, that the limit cycle is fixed, and that the sagittal and frontal planes can be studied separately. Here, we test these assumptions in seven public datasets of human gait (71 participants), including 16 people who both walked and ran. We fit linear step-to-step maps and validate them by cross-validation, holding out more data where more data exist. At first sight, gait has memory: the state two steps back lowers the prediction error by up to 29\%. Yet most of this temporal coupling vanishes once the operating point may drift slowly and measurement noise is modelled; gait remains limit-cycle-like, around an operating point that moves. Running keeps more memory than walking in the same people. Spatial coupling between the planes is present in most participants, mainly from sagittal to frontal, but weak. This supports planar models of healthy gait, while a repeatable, task-dependent coupling index may serve as a measure of gait quality. The simple models are wrong, but useful enough.

papers.title: AVID: A Weakly Aligned RGB-Infrared Dataset and Perturbation Benchmark for Tiny Aerial Targets
papers.abstract: Long-range detection of small drones is complicated by their visual similarity to birds and by the limited detail available from ground-based cameras. Combining visible and infrared observations offers complementary information, but their usefulness depends on target size, cross-modal alignment, and image quality. We present AVID, a benchmark for studying these factors using real RGB-infrared bird-drone surveillance footage originating from the Drone Detection Dataset and curated for the IEEE ICIP 2025 Video and Image Processing Cup. AVID comprises 32,040 corresponding frame pairs from 115 videos, with 35,952 existing bird and drone annotations at $320\times256$ resolution. Targets occupy an unusually narrow size range: 68.1\% have a geometric-mean bounding-box side of 8--16 pixels, and 99.0\% meet the COCO small-object criterion. To characterize the geometric difficulty of combining the modalities, we introduce an object-relative alignment ratio and an alignment burden curve. In a sample of 300 frame pairs, 32.3\% have estimated global translations greater than 5 pixels; among the 264 pairs with matching annotations, 16.3\% exceed one median target side. We further introduce AVID-C, which simulates seven families of image degradation at five severity levels independently in RGB, infrared, or both. A fixed-feature analysis examines how scale, degradation, and added cross-modal shifts affect fitted bird-drone class overlap. At 12--16 pixels, the Bhattacharyya error bounds are 0.148 for RGB, 0.198 for infrared, and 0.046 for their combined features. These values describe separation in the specified feature and density models, not detector accuracy. Together, AVID and AVID-C support scale-aware, alignment-aware, and sensor-specific studies of tiny aerial targets.

papers.title: Uniformization of compact Kähler Threefolds of Zero Kodaira Dimension
papers.abstract: Given two smooth compact Kähler threefolds $X$ and $Y$ whose universal covers are biholomorphic, we show that $κ(X) = 0$ if and only if $κ(Y) =0$.

papers.title: Scientist Mothers Working in Childcare Deserts Are Less Likely to Attain Tenure
papers.abstract: Childcare shortages have limited families' access to quality care, with consequences for children's development and parents' careers. We link two decades of childcare supply data to longitudinal surveys of U.S. scientists. We find workplace childcare deserts are widespread: more than half of scientists at universities and research institutions work in deserts, where supply falls significantly short of demand. We further find mothers working in deserts are less likely to attain tenure. They are also more likely to move to industry and part-time positions. Reduced work time partly accounts for the tenure association but other reasons remain. Expanding childcare availability near workplaces may help retain scientific talent.

papers.title: Characteristics of VHF and UHF band detection using Stark shifting in Rydberg-atom sensors
papers.abstract: We present a characterization of the sensitivity of broadband electric field measurements in the Very High Frequency (VHF) and Ultra High Frequency (UHF) bands using AC stark shifting of Rydberg states. The dependence of the sensitivity and dynamic range of the field measurements using nD5/2 states of cesium for principal quantum numbers n= 60, 70, 80, 90 and 100 is presented, detailing the intricacies involved. The frequencies considered for the measurement range from 50 MHz to 900 MHz for which a transverse electromagnetic (TEM) cell is used to excite the Rydberg atoms with the RF fields. The relative sensitivities achieved for various principal quantum numbers are presented. A general trend of better sensitivity for higher principal quantum numbers is observed. This work paves the way for a better understanding of the AC Stark dependent field measurements using Rydberg sensors.

papers.title: Variational surface matching for multichannel molecular photoionization
papers.abstract: We present an improved method for computing multichannel scattering states in the \ASTRA{} (AttoSecond TRAnsitions) molecular ionization code. Our pole-free Galerkin method with variational surface matching (PFG-VSM) yields a boundary response that is stationary with respect to errors in the interior wave function. Compared with matching based on directly evaluated radial derivatives, this formulation yields substantially faster convergence and greater numerical stability as the number of open channels increases. Comparison with a numerical solution of the exactly separable $\mathrm H_2^+$ problem establishes the accuracy attainable in a hybrid Gaussian--B-spline basis for a polycentric potential, independently of many-electron close-coupling approximations. A direct comparison of the two matching prescriptions for CO demonstrates the stability of the variational formulation under radial-basis coarsening. For neon, agreement with the NewStock atomic ionization code tests the treatment of the continuum degeneracies that arise when rotational symmetry is represented in $D_{2h}$. The excellent agreement with the independent \XCHEM{} molecular ionization code for CO partial cross sections and molecular-frame photoelectron angular distributions, both away from and across resonances, is a strong confirmation of the correctness of both codes. A comparison for pyrazine extends this validation to a larger polyatomic target.

papers.title: CAMEL: Cross-Architecture Masked Embedding Learning for Ultra-Lightweight Retinal Foundation Models
papers.abstract: Recent progress in deep learning has substantially advanced automated grading of ophthalmologic pathologies, supported by large annotated datasets and improved representation learning. However, a significant gap remains between state-of-the-art performance and clinical scalability. In particular, foundation models have reshaped image-based medical screening and diagnosis. These large-scale architectures trained on extensive datasets learn rich, generalizable feature representations that can be adapted to a wide range of downstream tasks. In ophthalmology, RETFound, one of the most relevant foundation models for retinal images, performs strongly across classification, segmentation, and risk prediction tasks. Despite their effectiveness, foundation models are often computationally prohibitive, hindering their deployment in real-world clinical environments where hardware constraints and latency are critical. To bridge this gap, we introduce CAMEL (Cross-Architecture Masked Embedding Learning), a novel cross-architecture distillation framework that uses an asymmetric masking strategy during embedding learning to effectively transfer knowledge from massive teacher foundation models to compact, lightweight student models. Our experimental evaluation across four datasets shows that CAMEL preserves accuracy while drastically reducing computational complexity, enabling lightweight yet highly accurate models suitable for resource-limited clinical settings.

papers.title: A Mixed $H_{\infty}$--Passivity Approach for Leveraging Heat-Pump-Connected District Heating Systems as Frequency Support in Electric Power Systems
papers.abstract: Heat-pump (HP)-connected district heating systems (DHSs) can support grid frequency by rapidly modulating HP electrical consumption while accommodating the resulting heat imbalance. Thermal-state-informed HP control improves EPS--DHS coordination, but introduces slower DHS dynamics and heat-side disturbance propagation at the electrical interface on the time scale of secondary frequency control. This paper formulates the regulated DHS as a grid-facing dynamic port and develops a mixed $H_\infty$--passivity framework for disturbance-independent temperature regulation while preserving a clean electrical response during secondary frequency control. Sufficient conditions guarantee local asymptotic stability of the EPS--HP--DHS interconnection across primary frequency control, secondary frequency control, and DHS regulation. These stability conditions are integrated with multi-channel $H_\infty$ attenuation of DHS-state-dependent electrical dynamics, heat-disturbance propagation, and DHS-regulation errors, yielding a tractable convex LMI program for controller synthesis. Cross-model validation deploys controllers synthesized on control-oriented EPS--DHS models, without retuning, on an open-source electromechanical IEEE 39-bus model coupled with four high-fidelity finite-volume DHS models retaining thermal transport, storage, and heat-loss dynamics. The resulting controller improves EPS--DHS coordination without compromising the grid-facing electrical response.

papers.title: Monte Carlo Random Walk Kernel
papers.abstract: We introduce the Monte Carlo Random Walk Kernel (MCRWK), an estimator whose per-pair cost is independent of graph size and derived directly from the random walk kernel (RWK) expansion. By normalizing the kernel coefficients, MCRWK samples a shared walk length and estimates its contribution using random walks on the input graphs. This gives a simple way to approximate RWK without constructing the product graph. For a fixed expected walk length and efficient neighbor sampling, each pairwise estimate takes $O(m)$ time for $m$ Monte Carlo samples, allowing the sample budget to control the trade-off between runtime and accuracy. We evaluate MCRWK against Graph Voyagers and classical RWK methods on synthetic and real graph datasets. In the reported experiments on large synthetic graphs, MCRWK is faster than Graph Voyagers and, at matched runtime, more accurate. It also has the lowest Gram-matrix runtime on the five real datasets studied. Code and experiments are available at https://github.com/arslan-yam/random_walk_kernels_computations

papers.title: On lens spaces which may embed in the complex projective plane
papers.abstract: Using an obstruction derived by Owens and relying on Donaldson's Diagonalisation Theorem, we obtain a complete classification of lens spaces of Lisca type $(2)$ or $(3)$ that are unobstructed from embedding in a homology complex projective plane. This classification is further refined for lens spaces $L(p,q)$ with $p$ even, using an obstruction due to Lidman--Moore--Vazquez based on work of Lin. This article is extracted from the author's PhD thesis.

papers.title: Optimizing Prompt Radio Counterpart Searches for Gravitational-Wave Events with the Deep Synoptic Array
papers.abstract: Prompt millisecond-duration coherent radio emission is proposed as a counterpart to neutron-star-containing compact mergers, produced before, during, or shortly after coalescence. Its detection would probe the plasma environment, magnetic fields, remnant evolution, and emission physics of these mergers. At GHz frequencies, dispersive delays can range from fractions of a second to several seconds, requiring the telescope to be on source before or soon after coalescence. Negative- or low-latency alerts, rapid response, and optimized pointing under uncertain, evolving localizations are therefore essential. We present a framework for prompt gravitational-wave follow-up with the upcoming Deep Synoptic Array (DSA), a sensitive, fast-slewing, wide-field GHz radio array. We simulate low-latency localization sequences and embed them in a follow-up environment with elevation, field-of-view, and slew constraints. We compare a reinforcement-learning pointing policy with a baseline that slews toward the highest-probability accessible region at each step. This peak-tracking rule is a strong, interpretable baseline for initial deployment, while the learned policy provides a complementary strategy for a subset of broad, multimodal, or arc-shaped localizations. At a random merger time, 37% of events are observable above $20^\circ$ elevation; among these, $\sim90\%$ of BNS events are successfully reached and tracked using zero-noise localization maps, decreasing to $\sim75\%$ with Gaussian-noise maps. We validate the optimized pointing trajectories on prototype DSA antennas. DSA follow-up can reach a fluence sensitivity of $\sim20$ mJy ms over a representative 700-1025 MHz sub-band, probing millisecond bursts with luminosities of approximately $10^{38}$ to $10^{39}$ erg s$^{-1}$, at or below the lower end of several coherent-emission predictions for neutron-star mergers.

papers.title: P-ContextBench: From Personal Fact Recall to Personalized Agent Behavior
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used for personal tasks, yet evaluating their safe use of personal context remains difficult because such contexts are private, fragmented, dynamic, and socially situated. We introduce P-ContextBench, a realistic, verifiable, and scalable benchmark for evaluating personal-context understanding. P-ContextBench constructs population-structured, life-story-grounded digital humans from demographic seeds reflecting the U.S. population. Rather than using explicit, static profiles, P-ContextBench embeds traits, routines, goals, and constraints as implicit evidence across fragmented, evolving synthetic mobile-app records. It evaluates five capabilities: single-source fact recovery, multi-source fact recovery, temporal state tracking, inference of higher-level personal patterns from routine behavior, and safe handling of requests conflicting with persona-specific constraints through compliance, warning, clarification, or refusal. A multi-stage validation pipeline checks persona plausibility, context recoverability, information leakage, evidence preservation, test-case grounding, and human-judge agreement. We instantiate P-ContextBench with 100 personas, 10,088 hidden facts, 18,261 app-trace fragments, and 4,810 verified test cases. The pipeline supports configurable generation across scales and demographic groups. Cost-effective state-of-the-art (SOTA) LLMs relevant to personal agents achieve below 60% accuracy on temporal tracking, higher-level pattern inference, and constraint-aware action-boundary decisions, with fewer than 10% of test cases answered correctly across all three repeated runs. Even a high-performing SOTA model remains inconsistent on these capabilities. P-ContextBench provides measurable targets for improving the accuracy, reliability, and safety of LLM-based personal agents.

papers.title: Nondegeneracy of low-energy nodal solutions to the Yamabe equation
papers.abstract: We study the linearized Yamabe equation in $\R^n$, or equivalently on $\s^n$, at a low-energy sign-changing solution with two nodal domains. We consider odd dimensions $n=2k-1$ and a solution invariant under $Γ=O(k)\times O(k)$. Its regular level sets are isoparametric hypersurfaces, which foliate the sphere away from the two focal submanifolds. This symmetry reduces the equation for the solution to a singular ODE. In the balanced case, we choose a single-node profile that is odd under reflection across the midpoint. We prove nondegeneracy in the $Γ$-invariant subspace for every $k\ge2$, and in the full space $H^1(\s^n)$ for sufficiently large $k$: every kernel element is generated by a conformal invariance of the equation. The proof uses separation of variables, Wronskian identities and comparison functions adapted to the singular equations for the angular modes.

papers.title: Renegotiable Options Fail to Prevent Hold-Up Between Two Profit-Maximizing Frontier LLM Agents
papers.abstract: Do contract terms that protect investment between people also protect it between profit-maximizing language-model agents? In the hold-up problem, a seller can adapt a unit to one buyer at a cost before the price is set. Once that cost is sunk, the buyer can offer almost nothing and the seller will still accept, so a seller who foresees this does not adapt. One remedy is an option: the buyer may buy at a fixed price. In theory the option stops working if the buyer can let it lapse and offer its own price instead. Yet in a laboratory experiment by Hoppe and Schmitz, this renegotiable option raised human investment from 41.5% of pairs without a contract to 67.2%. We had Claude Opus 5.5 and GPT-6.1 Sol, each told to maximize its side's profit, play a one-shot game with the same strategic structure under their four contract regimes and a reference-price control. The agents did what game theory predicts: under the renegotiable option no seller adapted, and under the option that rules out this renegotiation every seller did. In a second experiment in which sellers no longer stated their expected revenue before deciding, removing the profit instruction left investment unchanged under no contract and both options. When we changed the numbers so that the buyer would exercise the option even without adaptation, adapting only added cost, and no seller adapted: the agents did not simply adapt whenever an option was offered or whenever its price covered the cost. Under our protocol, a contract term that raised investment between people did not protect it between agents.

papers.title: Isometric Embeddings of Asymptotically Hyperbolic Manifolds into Hyperbolic Space
papers.abstract: The Nash Embedding theorem asserts that every closed Riemannian manifold can be isometrically embedded into a Euclidean space of sufficiently high dimension. In this paper, we address the asymptotically hyperbolic version of the problem. We prove that an asymptotically hyperbolic manifold $\left(M,g\right)$ can be realized as a submanifold of a sufficiently high-dimensional hyperbolic space $\mathrm{H}^{N+1}$, intersecting the sphere at infinity transversely, if and only if $g$ is asymptotically Poincaré-Einstein to second order.

papers.title: Existence and stability of Weyl points
papers.abstract: Weyl points are quasimomentum-energy pairs in the band structure of three-dimensional periodic media at which two dispersion surfaces touch conically. They first arose in a model introduced by H. Weyl in 1929, but were first observed only recently in condensed matter physics and photonics experiments. Weyl points have been explored theoretically via numerical computation and via tight binding (discrete) models. In this article we present the first analytical treatment of Weyl points in a continuum PDE-type model. Starting with a Schrödinger operator whose electric potential is periodic with respect to the body-centered cubic (BCC) lattice, we introduce a small BCC-periodic magnetic vector potential that is equivariant with respect to a specific abelian group of symmetries. For magnetic Schrödinger operators of this type, we prove (i) that a pair of Weyl points bifurcates from a threefold degeneracy in the band structure of the underlying non-magnetic operator, and (ii) that these Weyl points are stable against small self-adjoint BCC-periodic perturbations of both the electric and magnetic vector potentials.

papers.title: Completeness and dynamical stability in exoplanet occurrence rates
papers.abstract: Exoplanet population studies are often quantified through the "occurrence rate" of certain types of planet. This value can be calculated from a survey of a sample of stars by taking the "detection rate" and correcting with a completeness factor. This completeness is calculated via detection limits on each individual star, and can be calculated either individually for each detected planet or averaged in a certain area of parameter space. We test whether either the average completeness or individual completeness performs better than the other. We also test whether including dynamical stability constraints in the detection limits improves the occurrence rate results. We use synthetic sets of exoplanetary systems and calculate occurrence rates for each and compare to what the value would be with perfect information. We compare how close each method is to the ground truth to assess which is most suitable. Overall, in our synthetic sets, the average completeness is more reliable though it can be a problem if there is a sharp change in the underlying population within the area of parameter-space considered. We find that using dynamical stability conditions causes a bias in the occurrence rate and do not recommend using these.

papers.title: Spherical law for optimal layouts of random graphs
papers.abstract: Can the nodes of a random graph be placed in an auxiliary space $\mathbb{R}^{M}$ so that its connectivity becomes local? The spring electric layout is a standard algorithm to try to find such local graph layouts; we study it as a statistical-physics problem by considering the Gibbs ensemble of spring-electric layouts. For graphs with independent edges we solve the model exactly at large number of nodes $N$ and fixed embedding dimension $M$. The node positions obey a spherical law: they are uniformly distributed in an $M$-dimensional ball; for $M=2$ this is closely related to Girko's circular law. Crucially, the ground state energy is flat across all layouts with that density: an optimal layout for one graph is asymptotically optimal for any other. Optimal layouts of i.i.d. graphs are therefore frustrated liquids, macroscopically constrained but microscopically unoptimizable. We discuss relations to graph-partitioning, Laplacian eigenmaps, and dimensionality reduction, and outline how this harsh result breaks down for correlated graphs.

papers.title: Better Retrievers, Worse Labels: How Incomplete Relevance Judgments Distort Abstention Evaluation in Conversational RAG
papers.abstract: Conversational RAG benchmarks such as MTRAG and RETECO evaluate retrieval and generation end to end: each system answers from its own retrieval, so abstention must be scored against whether each retrieved context is sufficient. A convenient shortcut reads sufficiency off the relevance judgments and treats a context without gold documents as unanswerable. We re-run the official baselines exactly and test this shortcut on RECOR (RETECO track~2) with four retrievers (nDCG@10 from .18 to .59) and three Qwen3 readers. Two open LLM judges and a panel of four small open models label each context by content, and a model of another family audits 250 contexts blind, with adjudication. The stronger the retriever, the larger the share of no-gold contexts that still contain the answer (28\% to 72\%) and the lower the shortcut's precision (.68 to .10; .70 to .21 under the audit). A reader agrees: Qwen3-4B answers 62--67\% of these false misses correctly, against 23--30\% of no-gold contexts judged insufficient and 1\% with no documents. In most false misses, the answer comes from a hard negative mined for the same question, another turn's gold or a neighbouring chunk of the gold page. On MTRAG, whose judgments come from annotators, precision drops from .72 to .50. Under the shortcut, answerability AUROC is up to .19 too low, and the best sufficiency detector appears to be a retrieval score that never reads the documents. We release code, runs and labels, and recommend scoring refusals against content labels, not the presence of gold.

papers.title: Separating Fermion and Gauge Resonances with Species-Dependent Lightcones in Warped Geometry
papers.abstract: Extra-dimensional flavor models generally tie together the mass scales of gauge and fermion Kaluza--Klein modes. We show how species-dependent five-dimensional lightcones, which can be generated, for example, by a simple scalar profile, can separate these scales while preserving four-dimensional Lorentz invariance and any proposed extra-dimensional flavor structure. In two illustrative models on stabilized backgrounds, right-handed quark partners lie at 6.6--12 TeV with 30 TeV KK gluons, or a 5.5 TeV gluon lies below fermion partners above 10 TeV. We compare with deconstructed and three-brane models.

papers.title: Temperature Evolution of Magnon-Polarons in the van der Waals Antiferromagnet FePS$_3$
papers.abstract: Magnon polarons, hybrid excitations arising from magnon-phonon coupling, were investigated in the van der Waals antiferromagnet FePS3 using magneto-Raman scattering measurements at temperatures ranging from 4 K to the vicinity of the Néel temperature ($T_\mathrm{N}$ = 118 K). The lower Zeeman-split component of the magnon-like mode, tuned by the magnetic field toward the lower-energy phonon mode, exhibits an avoided crossing. The corresponding magnetic field decreases from approximately 13 T at 4 K to 5.6 T at 85 K, bringing the effect within reach of a standard laboratory magnet. A model of three coupled bosonic modes shows that the magnon-phonon coupling constant, approximately 2.7 cm$^{-1}$ at low temperatures, decreases significantly with increasing temperature, following a trend similar to the temperature-induced softening of the magnon mode. This decrease in magnon-phonon coupling is discussed in terms of a possible reduction in sublattice magnetization due to thermal fluctuations.

papers.title: Comparison of melanin subtypes using pump-probe microscopy
papers.abstract: Pump-probe microscopy (PPM) is used to probe excited state dynamics of endogenous chromophores to generate contrast that is unavailable in traditional forms of microscopy. Here we apply PPM to characterize melanin, a pigment central to photoprotection, skin and eye pigmentation, and melanoma pathogenesis. Melanin is notoriously difficult to analyze due to its structural and chemical complexity. We imaged melanin from six different lesion categories: cutaneous nevi, lentigo, cutaneous malignant melanoma, conjunctival melanocytic lesions, vulvar melanocytic lesions, and a murine melanoma model, across 21 independent biological samples and 109 regions of interest. Using model fitting, adapted phasor analysis, and support vector machine classification, we characterize and quantify excited-state dynamics as a surrogate for chemical and structural heterogeneity. Heterogeneity of melanin separates cutaneous from non-cutaneous lesions, but is not correlated with malignancy. Benign lentigo is the most heterogeneous population in the dataset, exceeding cutaneous malignant melanoma, while conjunctival lesions are the most homogeneous despite receiving direct solar exposure. Classification on full transient absorption curves separates most subtypes well above the six-class chance level. These findings demonstrate the ability of PPM to reveal subtle differences in melanin photophysics across diverse tissue environments, with implications for optical tissue classification and the understanding of melanoma pathogenesis.

papers.title: Nedimo: An Evidence-Grounded Multilingual Pipeline for AI-Generated Sleep Stories
papers.abstract: Generative audio systems can produce large libraries of personalized bedtime content, but ordinary media objectives (retention, completion, and novelty) are poorly aligned with the goal of supporting a transition toward sleep. Direct evidence for narrated bedtime audio in adults is mixed, and a recent active-controlled trial did not support such audio as a standalone treatment for sleep disturbance. We translate this uncertain evidence into conservative engineering requirements and present a multilingual pipeline for generating and narrating low-arousal sleep stories. The implemented prototype separates deterministic planning from large language model generation, represents content and delivery parameters explicitly, shapes each script through a four-phase attention taper, validates structural and lexical constraints, performs a bounded error-aware retry, and quarantines unresolved outputs. Provider-agnostic text-to-speech synthesis is followed by paragraph-aware joining, two-pass loudness normalization, and a publication gate that re-measures the saved, encoded file against fixed loudness, loudness-range, and true-peak limits. The product data model records stop position, replay, early abandonment, and completion while treating these events as ambiguous behavioral proxies rather than clinical outcomes. We contribute an evidence-to-requirement mapping, a traceable guardrail architecture with explicit acceptance thresholds, technical evaluation criteria, and a prospective protocol for testing sleep-onset effects. No clinical efficacy is claimed; the system is positioned as a relaxation and attentional-support tool whose benefit and possible reliance must be evaluated empirically.

papers.title: FieldGuideRAG: Image-Grounded GraphRAG for Fine-Grained Recognition with Vision-Language Models
papers.abstract: We present FieldGuideRAG, a training-free GraphRAG method in which a vision-language model, or VLM, recognizes fine-grained species by comparing the query with real photographs stored on the nodes of a knowledge graph. Multimodal GraphRAG systems describe each entity in text, and text conveys little of the visual detail that separates look-alike species. Our graph stores one photograph on every species node and links each species to its relatives, its geographic range and its ecological facts. A frozen VLM verifies the query against the photograph of each candidate node. FieldGuideRAG fuses the verification scores with the range edge and answers questions about the organism from the fact edges of the verified species. On CUB-200, a Wikidata graph and four iNaturalist domains, the node photograph improves verification over the species name on every graph, while text descriptions add little. Verification of the candidate pool exceeds a SigLIP retriever by up to 16 points, the range edge adds 7 to 19 points on iNaturalist, and answering from fact edges is correct on up to 89.5% of 28,820 ecological questions. The verification scores also detect queries whose species is missing from the graph. Graphs, prompts and code will be released.

papers.title: TalkFlow: Structured Latent Flow Matching for Speech Driven Holistic Motion Generation
papers.abstract: Holistic co-speech motion generation aims to synthesize coordinated facial expressions, hand gestures, and body movements from speech, which is challenging due to heterogeneous part-specific dynamics, long-range temporal coherence, and cross-part coordination. Directly modeling high-dimensional motion can be unstable, while overly compact or unstructured latent spaces may lose fine-grained motion details. We present \textbf{TalkFlow}, a structured latent flow framework for speech-driven holistic motion generation. TalkFlow learns a continuous three-stream latent representation for upper-body motion, lower-body motion, and facial expressions, preserving part-specific dynamics without forcing heterogeneous motion components into a single latent space. To maintain holistic coordination, lightweight cross-stream interactions are incorporated in both latent representation learning and flow-based generation. Conditioned on multi-level speech features, TalkFlow performs speech-conditioned latent flow matching, learning a continuous transport process from source latents to realistic motion latents. Experiments on the BEAT2 dataset demonstrate strong performance across facial expression accuracy, body gesture quality, and speech-motion synchronization. Qualitative comparisons and user studies further show that TalkFlow generates more natural, expressive, and speech-aligned holistic motion than state-of-the-art methods. The project page is available at https://xinmuwang.github.io/TalkFlow/.

papers.title: RADI3N: GeometRic ImAge EDiting via ParametrIc 3D CoNtrol
papers.abstract: Recent diffusion-based methods have substantially advanced image editing, yet parametric 3D control at the part level remains challenging. Existing approaches either operate on whole objects with manual rigging, or revert to 2D handles at the part level. They also struggle to model appearance and texture under large transformations, leading to unrealistic outputs in geometry-intensive edits. To address these limitations, we introduce RADI3N, a framework for semantically-grounded part-aware object manipulation with parametric 3D control. Our CS-ARAP deformation module suppresses rotation-field discontinuities at part boundaries via neighborhood covariance smoothing, producing structurally consistent deformations under complex part-level edits. We further introduce an inversion-free selective texture transfer mechanism that suppresses high-frequency positional biases and scales up low-frequency semantic cues within cross-image attention. This eliminates strict spatial bias and supports semantic matching, allowing source appearance to follow the edited part onto its new geometry. Experiments demonstrate that RADI3N achieves state-of-the-art performance in geometric fidelity, viewpoint consistency, and controllability.

papers.title: Fewer Heads, Fewer Memories: Pruning Redundant Attention Heads Suppresses Verbatim Memorisation
papers.abstract: Large language models have been shown to memorise and reproduce verbatim sequences from their training data, raising concerns about privacy leakage, intellectual property exposure, and the limits of generalisation. Recent theoretical work suggests that attention heads may contribute to this behaviour by functioning as associative memory mechanisms, with memorisation capacity scaling with the number of heads. At the same time, empirical work has shown that many attention heads are redundant and can be pruned with limited impact on downstream performance. Despite these parallel findings, the effect of pruning redundant heads on memorised-sequence reproduction remains unexplored. In this work, we demonstrate that zeroing out a substantial fraction of attention heads prior to inference can significantly suppress verbatim memorisation while preserving, or even improving, language modelling performance on the benchmark used to identify redundant heads. Evaluating GPT-2-XL(1.5B) on known memorised sequences, we find that pruning 729 task-redundant heads reduces the memorisation count by 91.5%, while improving WikiText-103 perplexity by 0.92. These findings suggest that attention-head redundancy can be exploited to mitigate memorisation at inference time, without retraining or modifying the training data.

papers.title: Does Showing Agents the Privilege of Their Tools Reduce Over-Privileged Tool Selection?
papers.abstract: When several tools can complete a task, an agent that picks the most powerful one holds more authority than the task needs. Recent work demonstrates that language-model agents do this often, and more so after a tool fails. Approaches to restrict focus so far on either enforcing least privilege outside the model or retraining the model. We ask a simpler question: does it help to tell the agent what each tool's privilege is? To investigate this question, we run all 544 ToolPrivBench scenarios on eight models, three run locally, and five through a hosted API, under five conditions: (1) no signal, (2) a least-privilege instruction, (3) privilege class and cost shown in each tool description, (4) both the instruction and privilege information, and (5) a matched neutral-metadata control. Showing privilege lowers premature escalation on every model that over-privileges at a measurable rate, reducing over-privileged selection by up to 19.3 percentage points (50\%), whereas irrelevant metadata in the same format does not. On most models, however, information alone mainly delays escalation until the standard tools have been tried. Combined with the instruction it more often avoids escalation, and the share of scenarios completed without a risk tool rises on seven of the eight models, reaching 51.1\% safe completion from a baseline of 18.8\% on the strongest-performing configuration. Visible privilege is therefore a cheap complement to enforcement rather than a substitute.

papers.title: Dynamic Skinning: Kinematics-Driven Cartoon Effects for Articulated Characters
papers.abstract: We present an extension to traditional rig skinning, like Linear Blend Skinning (LBS), to produce secondary motions that exhibit the appearance of physical phenomena without need for simulation. At the core of the technique, we call dynamic skinning, is a set of deformers which offset position of individual vertices as a function of position derivatives and time. Examples of such deformers create effects such as oscillation in response to movement and the appearance of wave propagation, among others. Because the technique computes offsets directly and does not solve physics equations, it is extremely fast to compute. It also boasts a high degree of customizability which supports a desirable artist workflow and fine level of control. Finally, we showcase the technique in a number of scenarios and make comparisons with the state of the art.

papers.title: Learning the Omega-Limit Partition from Approximate Koopman Invariants
papers.abstract: Nonlinear dynamical systems with multiple omega-limit sets pose a fundamental challenge for global finite-dimensional Koopman modeling with continuous observables. A natural way to address this challenge is to decompose the state space into forward-invariant regions associated with distinct asymptotic behaviors and to learn a separate Koopman model for each region. This paper studies how to compute such partitions from data. We establish conditions under which Koopman-invariant observables, namely eigenfunctions associated with the unit eigenvalue, characterize the stationary partition induced by omega-limit sets. Building on this characterization, we develop OPAL (Omega-limit Partitions from Approximate invariants Learned from data), an algorithm that extracts partitions from approximate invariant observables. Numerical examples show that the recovered partitions capture the relevant asymptotic regions and support multiple regional linear Koopman models with significantly improved long-horizon prediction capabilities.

papers.title: Connes spectral distance as a quantum distance measure and a geometric measure of entanglement
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study the Connes spectral distance as a quantum distance measure and its applications in discriminating quantum states and calculating quantum entanglement. Based on finite matrix algebra, we construct a spectral triple for finite dimensional quantum states. The Connes spectral distance is a generalization to the quantum trace distance and Hilbert-Schmidt distance. The corresponding optimal elements can always be chosen to commute with the difference matrix $Δ$, and then the optimal element and $Δ$ can be simultaneously diagonalized. We obtain the formulas of Connes spectral distances in three different parameter regimes which depending on the spectrum of difference matrix. As applications, we show how to use spectral distances to distinguish state pairs that have the same trace distance and Hilbert-Schmidt distance. We also define a new geometric measure of entanglement based on spectral distance. These results can help us study the relationships among Connes spectral distance, quantum trace distance and other quantum distance measures. These concrete constructions are significant for studies of quantum states in the framework of noncommutative geometry.

papers.title: Microscopic Theory of Spin-Orbit Interactions of Light
papers.abstract: Optical spin-orbit interactions (SOI), demonstrated experimentally in optical cavities, enable the polarization degrees of freedom of light to be described and controlled as an effective pseudospin, providing a foundation for spintronic-like control of light and the development of next-generation optical technologies. However, prior works describe this emergent effect using phenomenological models that fail to uncover its microscopic quantum origins, and as a result, a rigorous connection between material electronic structure and the optical SOI remains elusive. In this work, we address this fundamental challenge by developing a microscopic quantum theory starting from the non-relativistic quantum electrodynamical (QED) description of light-matter interactions. We show that this effect arises from virtual interactions between confined photons and material excitations. Crucially, our theoretical framework provides microscopic material-design principles for tuning the distinct components of optical SOI, which include the optical birefringence, photonic self-energies, TE-TM splitting, and optical Zeeman splitting, enabling precise engineering of effective magnetic fields, diabolical points, and pseudospin textures. We anticipate that the predictive capability of our microscopic theory will enable systematic screening and design of material systems for photonic spintronics and optical technologies.

papers.title: Martingale Representation in Counting-Process Filtrations via Poisson Embedding
papers.abstract: We revisit martingale representation for counting processes using the Poisson embedding, deriving the representation in their natural filtration from that of the underlying Poisson random measure. Our approach combines Poisson Malliavin calculus with the Clark-Ocone and Mecke formulas. We first characterize measurability with respect to the counting-process filtration through the structure of the Malliavin derivative. We show that any random variable measurable in the counting-process filtration is invariant with respect to the auxiliary mark on the acceptance region obtained from the Poisson embedding method and vanishes on the rejection region. We then prove that every square-integrable martingale in this smaller filtration consequently admits a unique stochastic integral representation with respect to the compensated counting process: the integrand is explicitly characterized as the conditional expectation of the Malliavin derivative, which identifies as the conditional effect of an additional accepted event on the terminal functional. Additionally, we define the mirroring counting process which counts the rejected events in the Poisson embedding procedure and we then provide an orthogonal decomposition of any martingale in the joint filtration of the accepted and rejected counting processes as a sum of a martingale in the counting filtration obtained by Poisson embedding and its mirroring martingale part on the rejected domain. Finally, we apply these results to general Hawkes processes constructed by Poisson embedding, obtaining a martingale representation and an explicit integrand formula in their natural filtration.

papers.title: Towards Elastic Least Privilege for Agent Planning
papers.abstract: General-purpose AI agents require authority that changes between tasks and during execution. Common deployments trade broad permissions that expose unnecessary authority and narrow permissions that raise approval requests. Existing mechanisms can enforce dynamic authority, but agent tool interfaces rarely provide the agent's planner, the component that chooses its actions, a means of comparing the authority required by alternative actions or of seeing the cost of the authority it already holds. Drawing on the rich history of access control research, we propose the concept of \emph{elastic least privilege}, in which an agent begins with a small baseline of authority and may acquire more within an owner-defined envelope. Elevations are leased and measured against a replenishing budget. Their cost increases with power, proximity to mandatory safety invariants, and repeated requests. Costs are visible to the planner, which can prefer lower-privilege choices and release authority it no longer needs. Authority returns automatically to the baseline when a lease expires, when it is released, or when the budget is exhausted, while persistent legitimate demand may prompt an owner-approved change to the baseline. Building on prior risk-priced and budget-aware access control, we redesign these mechanisms for agents. How best to implement the approach and how well it works in practice are open research questions. In this paper, we present how the approach could work, illustrate the model, and set an open research agenda.

papers.title: Strong Lower Bounds for Weak Epsilon-Nets
papers.abstract: Let $P$ be a finite point set in $\mathbb{R}^d$. A weak $\varepsilon$-net for $P$ with respect to convex sets is a finite set $X\subset\mathbb{R}^d$ intersecting every convex set containing at least $\varepsilon|P|$ points of $P$. Determining their optimal worst-case size was described by Alon, Kalai, Matousek, and Meshulam [Adv. Appl. Math., 2002] as "one of the truly important open problems in combinatorial geometry." We give elementary constructions which establish the first polynomially superlinear lower bounds in fixed dimension. Already in $\mathbb{R}^3$, we construct point sets for which every weak $\varepsilon$-net has size $Ω(\varepsilon^{-3/2})$. More generally, for every fixed $d\ge3$, we obtain a lower bound of $Ω_d(\varepsilon^{-γ_d})$, where $γ_d=\sqrt{d/2}+O(1)$. Consequently, no upper bound of the form $O_d(\varepsilon^{-C})$ can hold with an absolute constant $C$ which is independent of the dimension. Despite the recent progress on upper bounds, the strongest previous general lower bound remained $Ω_d(\varepsilon^{-1}\log^{d-1}(1/\varepsilon))$, due to Bukh, Matousek, and Nivasch [Israel J. Math., 2011]. To obtain our results, we apply a quadratic lift to grid-based configurations with many point-line incidences. The bounds also yield polynomial separations between fractional and integral piercing numbers of convex families, and lower bounds for Hadwiger-Debrunner numbers.

papers.title: LLM Fine-Tuning Workloads: Characterization, Challenges, and Opportunities for Serverless AI
papers.abstract: Serverless execution of Large Language Models (LLMs) is becoming important, reflecting their wide societal use. An increasingly present stage in LLM pipelines is fine-tuning, which specializes trained models and improves inference performance. Serverless operation of LLM fine-tuning workloads shifts operational concerns from the user to the provider. For these new workloads, providers face important operational complexities, such as performance issues, resource waste, and even service failure due to misconfiguration. However, optimizing such workloads is still at an early stage, and, relevant to this work, relatively little is currently known about how LLM fine-tuning workloads run in practice. In this work, we address the knowledge gap by characterizing the execution of LLM fine-tuning workloads on clusters equipped with different GPUs, running LLM models at various scales. We analyze IBM's LLMFineTuningBench, a large-scale, diverse profiling dataset of 30,920 fine-tuning experiments that records both successful and failing configurations. We provide quantitative insight into throughput (expressed in tokens/s), scaling, failure, and potential for performance optimization for four commonly used GPU types, in setups of 1 to 32 GPUs. We find that (1) job feasibility (run or fail) depends on workload properties, with failure ratios rising from 52% for small batch sizes (16-64) up to 95% for the largest (1,024); (2) throughput grows logarithmically with batch size; (3) scaling is near-linear when the workload is deployed intra-node, and optimizations such as RoCE substantially improves efficiency for inter-node deployment (e.g., 0.72 vs. 0.26 efficiency without RoCE); and (4) system-level optimizations can outweigh application-level ones (RoCE, up to 2.9$\times$, vs. Fast MoE, 1.7$\times$).

papers.title: RC Prediction: A Python Package for Parameter-Aware Reservoir Computing
papers.abstract: A nonlinear dynamical system can be characterized by the autonomous evolution of its state in time and its dependence on system parameters. As a parameter varies, the dynamics can change quantitatively and, at bifurcation points, qualitatively. When the governing equations are unknown, a data-driven model should therefore capture both elements from observational data, rather than reproduce the dynamics at a single operating condition only. Parameter-aware reservoir computing (PARC) is a model-free framework for this purpose, where the parameter is supplied to a reservoir computer through an additional input channel. PARC is trained on time series recorded at several parameter values, and the trained reservoir, run in closed loop as an autonomous dynamical system, generates trajectories at parameter values that were never observed. rc_prediction is an open-source Python package that implements this workflow. It provides multi-parameter training of a reservoir, autonomous closed-loop prediction at user-specified parameter values, parameter scans, and a standard echo state network for forecasting at a fixed parameter. Hyperparameter optimization and optional GPU acceleration through PyTorch are also provided. We use three benchmark dynamical systems as examples to demonstrate its usage. As one of the featured applications, here we illustrate the prediction of critical transitions and system collapse: trained only on pre-critical data, the model is queried beyond the training range to predict whether the system collapses, to estimate the critical parameter $p_c^{*}$, and to characterize transient lifetimes.

papers.title: The psychophysics of affect in large language models
papers.abstract: Good decisions often require considering how outcomes will feel. Yet large language models (LLMs) increasingly enter decision workflows, despite little being known about how they map outcomes to feelings or use those mappings in choice. We tested how LLMs anticipated gambling or stock-trading outcomes would feel and whether they incorporated these ratings into choice. When outcomes were rated in isolation, ratings exhibited diminishing sensitivity to magnitude, resembling human value functions; but models rated gains more intensely than equivalent losses, an inversion of canonical loss aversion we call silicon gain amplification. When outcomes were rated together, enabling direct comparison, ratings linearised. In choice, the gain-loss asymmetry largely disappeared, and models' own ratings did not reliably explain their choices better than monetary utility did. These findings reveal malleable mappings from outcomes to affect, raising questions about whether and how agentic LLMs should incorporate anticipated feelings into decisions.

papers.title: Exact Electron Dynamics in Linear and Chiral Cavities: Complete Field versus Single-Helicity Reduction
papers.abstract: Can a chiral cavity turn a free electron into a Landau-like orbiting particle? We answer with exact solutions of three quadratic electron--cavity models in the dipole limit, valid at arbitrary coupling. A single linearly polarized mode dresses the electron mass, which delays its flight, slows the spreading of a wavepacket and entangles the packet with the cavity. The complete transverse field, with both circular helicities, keeps two commuting, gapless translations at any coupling, mode number and helicity splitting, so the electron stays ballistic and no synthetic magnetic field appears. Keeping a single helicity gives two inequivalent models that are not related by a gauge transformation: reducing before the Power--Zienau--Woolley transformation gives ballistic motion, whereas reducing after it gives a Landau-like crossed-quadrature Hamiltonian. They differ by a real uniform field $B=sλ^2/(2ω_c)$ ($ω_c$ the mode frequency, $λ$ the coupling, $s=\pm1$ the helicity). In the complete theory the frequency $ω_{-s}$ of the partner helicity, measured against $g^2=λ^2/(2ω_c)$, decides between them: the electron is ballistic for a stiff partner, and Landau-like only at the soft-partner point, through an exact canonical reorganization that holds for the active sector but not for observables such as the electron--photon entanglement. Projecting onto one helicity after the PZW transformation is therefore not by itself a mechanism for synthetic magnetism; the mode content of the cavity is.

papers.title: Handlebodies separate elements of surface groups
papers.abstract: In this note I prove that every non-trivial element of the fundamental group of a closed orientable surface X is non-trivial in the fundamental group of some handlebody with boundary X. This result appears to be folklore. I have uploaded a proof as the result is needed in a joint project with Clement Dupont on mapping class group actions on configuration spaces.

papers.title: Beyond the Federer paradox in tennis
papers.abstract: Roger Federer won about 80% of his professional matches with only 54% of the points. Hierarchical scoring amplifies small advantages on points into large advantages on matches, but also allows a player to win with fewer points than the opponent. Using Monte Carlo simulations and exact Markov chain calculations, we show that in tennis, badminton, volleyball and table tennis this amplification is set almost entirely by the number of points per match. We then let a player win ordinary points with probability p1 and crucial points, those closing a game, set or match, with probability p2. In every sport a narrow region of the (p1, p2) plane exists where a player wins most matches with fewer than half of the points, because crucial points carry more influence than their share of points. Of ATP matches played in 1991-2025, 4.7% were won with fewer points, 16% more than independent points predict (5% including the serve), a constant excess. Pressure performance measured in other seasons predicts match outcomes beyond the points won, and Fabio Fognini won 51% of his matches with 49% of the points, in what we call the Fognini paradox.

papers.title: Variational Programs with Open Clocks
papers.abstract: Variational quantum algorithms leave the durations of Hamiltonian evolutions open for a classical optimizer to set. We present VHamilton, a minimal extension of the Hamilton quantum programming language in which such durations are open clocks: one program denotes a family of Hamiltonian trajectories, and a valuation fills its clocks with exact dyadic times, so that each instance is an ordinary Hamilton program that compiles to circuits as before. Because the semantics stays exact and affine in the clocks, the Hamiltonian structure of a variational program remainsavail able for reasoning about every valuation at once. Equivalence becomes a finite calculation, which we mechanize in Agda for a fragment and use to prove the VHamilton form of the compiler rewrite "rzz(t) = cx; rz(t); cx" for every clock value. We then show what the same structure supports in a two-qubit chemistry eigensolver written in VHamilton and run through a Haskell prototype. It supports a fusion of commuting blocks, a closed form and an expressibility proof for the ansatz, and an exact split of the error between the precision of the target and that of the clocks, with a priori bounds. It also supports a coordinate search whose queries per sweep, fixed by the spectra of the generators, do not grow with the precision. On the benchmark this search reaches the numerically verified optimum of a grid of 134 million valuations in 53 energy queries. It finds the grid optimum in only 21 of 30 validation settings, however, so the gain is conditional, not a global-optimization guarantee.

papers.title: Hyperelliptic curves on $(1,d)$ abelian surfaces for $d\leq 15$
papers.abstract: Bryan, Oberdieck, Pandharipande and Yin predicted the number of hyperelliptic curves on general abelian surfaces under a transversality condition. Some of the numbers have already been confirmed. In this paper we construct singular hyperelliptic curves on $(1,d)$ polarised abelian surfaces for $d\leq 15$ confirming a few predicted numbers, namely of (geometric) genus $g=d$ and of geometric genus $k+3$ on $(1,2k)$ and $(1,2k+1)$ polarised surfaces. Moreover, we have found that all genus 7 hyperelliptic curves on general $(1,8)$ polarised surfaces are double coverings of curves locally embedded into $(1,4)$ polarised surfaces. More interestingly, there is a unique genus 9 hyperelliptic curve (up to translation) locally embedded into a general $(1,12)$ polarised surface and it is a Klein covering of a curve locally embedded into a $(1,3)$ polarised surface.

papers.title: Electron-electron interactions mediated by overdamped vibrations: Implications for chirality-induced spin selectivity
papers.abstract: Motivated by chirality-induced spin selectivity (CISS), we investigate spin polarization during molecular electron transfer through a correlated bridge in the presence of a rapidly relaxing Peierls mode. By modulating both electronic hopping and spin--orbit coupling, the mode mediates two-body spin-spin interactions, including isotropic, anisotropic, and Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya exchange. We derive these interactions using an exact Lang-Firsov transformation for a four-site chiral bridge. We then include fast vibrational relaxation in the joint electron--vibration master equation and derive the reduced electronic dynamics to second order in the vibronic coupling, retaining both coherent and dissipative contributions and the finite-time buildup of the vibrational response. We test our derivation by numerical simulations, finding spin polarization accumulated at the acceptor after unpolarized injection, with nonmonotonic dependence on damping and bridge filling. Within the postulated local-loss model, our results show that rapid vibrational relaxation does not preclude spin polarization through a correlated bridge and provide a framework for assessing vibration-mediated interactions and dissipative dynamics as ingredients of CISS in molecular electron transfer.

papers.title: A Temporal Cellular Sheaf Framework for Multi-Agent Systems with Switching Communication Topologies
papers.abstract: Cellular sheaves serve as a natural modeling framework for encoding heterogeneity in the state and interaction spaces of multi-agent systems. This work examines switching communication graphs with the use of temporal cellular sheaves, which we construct to represent heterogeneous agent state spaces, the maps that relate them, and their respective communication constraints. We then develop sufficient conditions under which a multi-agent system defined on a temporal cellular sheaf can solve the target tracking problem by generalizing the existing concept of joint connectivity. Using a Lyapunov-based stability analysis, we demonstrate that the target tracking error of the network converges to a neighborhood of the origin.

papers.title: Can Personal Requirements Become Supervision for Planning?
papers.abstract: Managing multiple chronic conditions through diet requires satisfying disease- and medication-specific requirements jointly across meals and days while preserving established eating habits. These requirements are public in clinical guidelines and drug labels, yet turning them into a feasible plan for one person remains difficult for language-model agents. In our dietitian-approved weekly planning evaluation built from NHANES, thirteen models, from medically fine-tuned 8B models to GPT-6.1 Sol, pass fewer than 3% of complete plans through direct generation. Explicit rules, higher reasoning effort, or model-directed tools leave GPT-6.1 Sol at no more than 8%. We present Noura, which pairs LLM planning with executable personal specifications instantiated from public clinical guidance and individual health and dietary profiles. During planning, the specification grounds foods, optimizes portions, checks the complete multi-day plan, and guides revision. Our key insight is that a specification that rejects a plan can also determine what to learn from it. Noura turns executed plans and contextually credited revisions into supervision for compact models, recovering targets even from trajectories that never achieve complete success. The same specification supplies supervised targets, preferences, and rewards for post-training. On 4,993 held-out participants, Noura-SFT raises Qwen3-14B's complete-plan pass rate from 24.0% to 72.5% within the same execution loop, cuts rule violations by 97.5% with no observed critical failures, and improves dietary quality. The locally hosted 14B planner incurs fewer rule violations than its GPT-6 Luna teacher. A matched comparison shows that executed targets reduce rule violations by 41% over model-written proposals. Across four Qwen, Phi, and Llama backbones, self-training alone reduces rule violations by 41-61% on a 1,249-person population subset.

papers.title: Complete Au-free Metallization Platform for UWBG Al$_{0.65}$Ga$_{0.35}$N channel MOS-HEMTs using Ti/Al/Ti Ohmic Contacts and Refractory TiN/Pt Gates
papers.abstract: Au-free ohmic contacts and refractory gate stacks are critical for integrating ultra-wide-bandgap (UWBG) Al-rich AlGaN transistors with Si-CMOS technology. In this work, we demonstrate, to our knowledge, the first complete Au-free metallization platform for Al$_{0.65}$Ga$_{0.35}$N-channel MOS-HEMTs, combining electron-beam-evaporated and sputtered Ti/Al/Ti ohmic contacts with sputtered TiN and Pt gate metals. The Ti/Al/Ti contacts achieved a contact resistance of approximately 7.5--7.7 $Ω\cdot$mm while being fully Au-free. This contact resistance is achieved using a 600 $^\circ$C anneal, substantially below the 850--950 $^\circ$C typically required for Au-capped Ti/Al/X/Au contacts on Al-rich AlGaN, indicating a reduced thermal budget and improved compatibility with silicon-CMOS foundries. TiN gates deliver drain-current density up to 450 mA/mm at $V_{\mathrm{th}} = -13$ V, whereas Pt gates shift $V_{\mathrm{th}}$ to -2.5 V with a reduced current drive of 220 mA/mm, reflecting the effects of gate work function. TiN-gated devices exhibit lower current degradation under pulsed operation and a higher critical breakdown field ($E_{\mathrm{c}} \approx 3.5$ MV/cm) than Pt-gated devices ($E_{\mathrm{c}} \approx 2.98$ MV/cm), measured without field plating at $L_{\mathrm{GD}} = 2.3$ $μ$m. Collectively, these results establish a low-thermal-budget, fully Au-free, CMOS-compatible metallization platform for high-performance Al-rich AlGaN UWBG power electronics.

papers.title: Steady conformally Kähler Ricci solitons with isoparametric potential
papers.abstract: We classify complete, non-compact, simply connected, irreducible four-dimensional steady gradient Ricci solitons that are globally conformally Kähler and have an isoparametric potential. The steady Ricci solitons are $U(2)$-invariant nuts on $\mathbb R^4$, including the Bryant and Cao solitons, and bolts on $\mathbb{S}^2 \times \mathbb R^2$ and on $\mathcal O(-m)\to\mathbb{CP}^1$. For each $m\ge3$ there is exactly one non-collapsed bolt. A key step, valid for Ricci solitons of every sign, is that away from the locally conformally flat case, the conformal factor is aligned with the potential function, which yields cohomogeneity-one symmetry.

papers.title: Linear Rank Nonincreasing and Preserving Maps between Matrix Spaces
papers.abstract: We classify linear maps $φ$ between possibly different rectangular matrix spaces over a field $\mathbb F$ with $|\mathbb F|\ge5$ such that $\operatorname{rank} φ(A)\le2$ whenever $\operatorname{rank} A\le2$. Every such map has one of six forms. If its image contains a matrix of rank greater than two, then $φ(A)=MAN$ or $φ(A)=MA^{\top}N$ for fixed matrices $M,N$. The remaining forms have images consisting entirely of matrices of rank at most two, including an exceptional form arising from $3\times3$ alternating matrices. As a consequence, we characterize linear maps preserving rank exactly two. We also prove that rank-$k$ preservation implies rank-$k$ nonincrease when $|\mathbb F|>k+2$, and that rank-$k$ nonincrease implies rank-$\ell$ nonincrease for every admissible $\ell\ge k$ when $|\mathbb F|>k+1$. The classification uses the fact that the Chow rank of the generic $3\times3$ determinant is five, connecting the rank preserver problem with product decompositions of polynomials.

papers.title: Do Open Language Models Invent Scripture? BILAL-BENCH: Benchmarking Islamic-Source Fabrication in Bengali
papers.abstract: When a language model invents a Qur'anic verse or hadith, it gives false authority to text that readers may treat as sacred. Existing Islamic hallucination benchmarks are largely Arabic and often closed-ended, while Bengali resources mainly study general-domain hallucination or factual knowledge. We introduce BILAL-BENCH, a 240-question expert-verified benchmark for open-ended Islamic-source fabrication in Bengali. It covers Qur'anic attribution, hadith, fiqh, contemporary issues, and adversarial false-premise prompts, and uses a two-axis rubric that separates source errors from assertiveness. We evaluate seven open-weight models from 1B to 120B on 1,680 double-annotated responses. Six of the seven models confidently fabricate on 79.3-95.3% of source-production questions, with no monotonic improvement from scale. Hadith provenance is the weakest category across models: only two of 315 responses are correct and correctly sourced. The two 8B BanglaLLaMA variants have similar confident-fabrication rates but different error profiles. Models vary far more in whether they withhold a claim they cannot support than in source accuracy: appropriate abstention or false-premise correction ranges from 6 to 46 responses across the benchmark, and does not track parameter count.

papers.title: Optimal design problems for the fractional $g$-Laplacian at prescribed energy level
papers.abstract: In this work we study two optimal design problems, of hard and soft obstacle type, in fractional Orlicz-Sobolev spaces. We also establish the connection between these problems, and finally we analyze the asymptotic behavior of the quotients $Λ_{s,μ}(α)/μ$ with respect to the energy level $μ$ at the endpoints $0$ and $+\infty$.

papers.title: Steering Vectors as a Training Signal in LLM Post-Training
papers.abstract: Steering vectors (SVs) are residual-stream directions that shift the behavior of LLMs when added to hidden states at inference time. While prior work has mainly used SVs as post-hoc controls, we ask whether the same directions can also guide parameter updates during post-training. We study this question across supervised learning, including SFT and distillation, and reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR). Our framework considers two intervention regimes: a hidden-state hook during teacher-forced supervised training, and an advantage-repair mechanism on wrong rollouts in GRPO. For each regime, we analyze three design axes, which are the steering direction, its placement, and the operation used to combine it with training. In supervised settings, SV injection improves over plain SFT and distillation, with gains scaling with the off-policy gap and reaching up to a $12\%$ improvement when distilling from thinking-mode teachers. These gains hold across three random seeds. In RL settings, applying a correctness-contrast direction as advantage repair on wrong rollouts, including otherwise zero-gradient all-wrong groups, recovers a learning signal that transfers to held-out math benchmarks and acts as a composable auxiliary signal that adds to existing zero-variance remedies such as entropy-aware advantage shaping. We further identify three failure boundaries. In detail, code generation can break the direction, cross-family layer transfer can break the placement, and inference-time application on an SV-trained checkpoint can break the intervention regime. Together, these results establish steering vectors as a conditional but effective training signal for LLM post-training. Our code is available here.

papers.title: A Robust Approach to Belief Mismatch in Non-cooperative Dynamic Games
papers.abstract: Game-theoretic models are increasingly used to describe multi-agent interactions in control and robotics applications. However, theoretical and computational complexity makes these models intractable in many dynamic, incomplete information scenarios. Recent work makes strong assumptions to reduce computational complexity: agents share sensor measurements with one another and maintain a common estimate of state uncertainty. Unfortunately, these assumptions enforce a degree of cooperation in generically noncooperative interactions. This paper takes the perspective of an ego agent seeking both computational tractability and robustness to unanticipated behavior of other agents due to mismatched state estimates from private---rather than shared---sensor measurements. To that end, we formulate the game theoretic planning problem in an augmented belief space with perturbed Bayesian dynamics that allows the ego to predict all agents' potentially divergent state estimates. These perturbations are chosen by a hypothetical adversary, ``nature,'' to reflect how non-ego agents' state estimates---based on measurements the ego agent will not see at runtime---may deviate from the ego's own belief. Ultimately, our approach can be understood in the spirit of classical H-infinity robust control, extended to noncooperative, stochastic dynamic games. We present a solver with polynomial-time iterations and conduct two experiments which show how robust belief space reasoning leads ego agents to proactively limit their future vulnerability to model misspecification of other agents' beliefs and actions, reducing performance degradation by over 48%.

papers.title: From proof of concept to practice: the next decade of artificial intelligence in metasurface photonics
papers.abstract: Over the past decade, artificial intelligence has learned to predict electromagnetic responses rapidly and generate high-performance metasurface designs. However, one question remains open: compared with conventional design workflows that contain no learned model, has it made the complete design workflow faster, and are the resulting devices better? We argue that the answer depends on the task. Reading 100 highly cited optical studies in depth, we distinguish the design tasks in which artificial intelligence is irreplaceable, clearly advantageous, or without clear advantage. In our view, the key to the next decade is not more successes in isolated tasks but making each success a foundation for the field, through shifts such as shared data, trained models, and physics written into learning. Whether artificial intelligence leaves lasting value in this field will depend on whether its benefits can be verified, its methods transferred, and its designs corrected by experiment.

papers.title: When Can Unlabeled Data Pools Replace Membership Queries?
papers.abstract: Membership queries let a learner label arbitrary points and give near-optimal $\tilde O(n\log(1/\eps))$ label complexity for halfspaces under every marginal. A pool learner may label only sampled points. We ask when unlabeled data can replace membership queries. For homogeneous halfspaces the answer depends only on the angular law of $X/\|X\|$. If this law assigns zero mass to every hyperplane through the origin and positive mass to every nonempty open set of directions together with its reflection, a pool learner uses $O(n\log^3n\log(n/(\epsδ)))$ labels, uniformly over all such marginals and targets, without density, moment, concavity or isotropy assumptions. The same label bound holds for non-homogeneous halfspaces under every marginal with full support and no mass on affine hyperplanes, including Gaussians. Dropping either angular assumption admits $Ω(1/\eps)$ pool versus $O(\log(1/\eps))$ membership-query separations, even with unlimited unlabeled data. The price is paid in unlabeled data: in dimension $n\ge3$, for every unlabeled budget fixed in advance, some marginal satisfying both assumptions forces $Ω(1/\eps)$ labels. For isotropic $s$-concave marginals in dimension $n\ge3$, unlimited pools keep logarithmic label rates for every finite $s$. With an unlabeled budget fixed in advance, class-uniform polylogarithmic rates hold exactly for $s>-1/(n+1)$, or $s>-1/n$ under central symmetry, and in the general class the optimal rate between these thresholds is $\tildeΘ(\eps^{-(n-2)/n})$. This extends the range $s\ge-1/(2n+3)$ of previous sample-based guarantees, in the realizable setting.

papers.title: Lengths of closed geodesics on random non-compact hyperbolic surfaces
papers.abstract: We study the asymptotic distribution of the number of primitive, closed geodesics on Weil-Petersson random hyperbolic surfaces with genus $g$ and $n(g)$ cusps, under various growth rates of $n(g)$ as $g\to\infty$. We prove that the limiting distribution is Poisson with parameter depending explicitly on the limit of $n(g)^2/g$. This work is inspired by that of Mirzakhani and Petri's on closed surfaces and Hide and Thomas when $g$ is fixed. Our proof relies on first order expansions for Weil-Petersson moduli space volumes in the $n(g)/g\to 0$ regime. We also obtain some new existence results for small Laplacian eigenvalues.

papers.title: Tunable Three-Body Interactions in Microwave-Shielded Polar Molecules
papers.abstract: We show that microwave shielding, which enables collisionally stable ultracold polar molecules, also leads to genuine nonadditive three-body interactions comparable to the shielding interaction itself. Their magnitude, sign, and geometrical dependence can be flexibly controlled through microwave parameters and orientation. Interaction strengths can reach the ten kilohertz-scale for ultrapolar molecules in typical optical lattices. The nonadditive three-body interactions can stabilize novel many-body phases, and should be accounted for in quantum simulation with microwave shielded molecules.

papers.title: MOSAIC: Addressing Disproportionate Task-Modality Dependencies via Modality-Partitioned Gradient Routing
papers.abstract: In multi-task settings, combining multiple modalities allows task representations to draw on signals that a single modality alone would not capture. However, individual tasks may depend disproportionately on particular modalities, a structure that conventional fusion-based architectures do not model explicitly, instead enforcing a unified representation space. Consequently, a task's gradients can affect parameters tied to modalities it barely relies on, leaving features that compromise between competing demands. Although prior work has explored task-weighting and loss-balancing strategies, their effectiveness is limited by the absence of explicit modality separation, preventing models from optimising each modality according to its task-specific importance. To address these limitations, we propose MOSAIC (MOdality-Separated Architecture with Inter-modal Cross-attention), which preserves unimodal representations while enabling controlled interaction between them, and uses modality-specific losses to route gradients to their corresponding partitions. On the Corpus of Everyday Japanese Conversation (CEJC), MOSAIC improves average macro-F1 by 7.4 points across four tasks with a 72% reduction in backbone parameters relative to a fusion-based baseline. Our results demonstrate that modality partitioning yields consistent gains across tasks while requiring far fewer backbone parameters than a fusion-based design.

papers.title: GRB 241113B: the first SVOM and EP gamma-ray burst A soft GRB likely seen on-axis, from soft X-rays to gamma-rays
papers.abstract: In 2024, two new missions were launched to detect high-energy transients. EP and SVOM aim to observe soft transients from X-ray rich gamma-ray bursts (XRR), X-ray flashes (XRF), to fast X-ray transients (FXT). GRB 241113B, the first soft gamma-ray burst (GRB) jointly detected by EP and SVOM from soft X-rays to gamma-rays (0.5--1000~keV). GRB 241113B has an $E^{obs}_{peak} \approx 35$ keV and a redshift (z) likely between 0.5 and 3.5, with $T_{90,γ} \approx 42$~s (4--30~keV). This burst can be classified as either an XRR or XRF, depending on the fluence ratio used. The afterglow is achromatic and featureless with a normal decay ($α\approx -1.40$). The prompt emission does not satisfy the shock-breakout relation, and thus a geometry comprised of a jet is preferred. However, the afterglow fitting favors a jet viewed on-axis dominated by synchrotron emission due to electrons in a slow cooling regime, interacting with a wind medium. The bulk Lorentz factor ($Γ$) indicates that the motion of the jet is ultrarelativistic ($Γ_{0}>100$), which discards the dirty fireball model. Hence, the jet baryon loading should be compatible with that of classical GRBs (C-GRBs). The prompt spectral properties of GRB 241113B ($α$, $E^{\mathrm{obs}}_{\mathrm{peak}}$, $E_{γ,iso}$) are comparable to those of XRFs/XRRs and are in the continuity of the C-GRB distributions, setting it apart from the extragalatic FXT population solely detected by EP. Hence, the SVOM mission, with the benefit brought by the instrument ECLAIRs with its high sensitivity and low energy threshold (at 4keV), is able to detect the potential $γ$-ray counterpart of soft transients also observed by EP and help to differentiate them from FXTs. The latter show the interest of the joint operation of both missions to better study the landscape of soft transients.

papers.title: The Berger conjecture for three dimensional manifolds
papers.abstract: A conjecture of Berger says that on a simply connected manifold all of whose geodesics are closed, all unit speed geodesics have the same shortest period.
